sources.says: Metzudat Zion says בליעל means 'without a yoke', people who threw off the yoke of heaven.

sources.quote: אמר רבי יהודה הלוי: מ״כ כי בליעל דרך תפלה אל יעלה והוא האויב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites Rabbi Yehuda Halevi: בליעל is said as a prayer, 'may he not rise', and it means the enemy.

18:11.headline: A cherub is named for a child
18:11.body: Metzudat Zion says a כרוב is an angel. He cites the sages, who read the name as כרביא, the Aramaic for 'a boy', because cherubs have a human form.

sources.quote: כרוב. מלאך ורז״ל אמרו כרביא (חגיגה י״ג) והוא תרגום של נער כי דמות אדם להנה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says a כרוב is an angel, and the sages said כרביא, the Aramaic for 'boy', since they have a human form.

18:11.headline: Who flies, God or the cherub? Maimonides says the cherub
18:11.body: Maimonides says flying is never said of God, since it is a motion of animals. In 'He rode on a cherub and flew', it is the cherub that flies, and the image means the event came fast.

sources.quote: השלמות המדומה הזו, כלומר תנועת התעופה, אינה מיוחסת לה׳ כלל
sources.says: Maimonides says the motion of flying is not ascribed to God at all.

sources.quote: כי הכרוב הוא אשר עף, והכוונה במשל הזה היא מהירות בואו של הדבר ההוא
sources.says: Maimonides says it is the cherub that flies, and the image means how fast the thing came.

sources.quote: וירכב - דרך משל, והטעם: רדת הגזירה במהירות בלי התמהמה ועיכוב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is an image for the decree coming down quickly, without delay.

18:12.headline: God hides in darkness: Maimonides says the darkness is ours
18:12.body: Maimonides says the prophets picture God hidden in cloud or darkness to teach that our physical nature blocks us from grasping Him. He cites this verse as one such image: what blocks us is the dullness of our own matter, not a darkness around God.

sources.quote: לדבר זה נרמז בכל ספרי הנביאים כשנאמר שאנו מוסתרים מה׳ והוא מוסתר מאיתנו בענן או בחושך
sources.says: Maimonides says all the prophets hint at this when they say we are hidden from God and He from us, by cloud or darkness.

sources.quote: להסב את תשומת הלב לכך שהמונע הוא עכירות העצם שלנו
sources.says: Maimonides says it is to point out that what blocks us is the dullness of our own substance.

sources.quote: משל זה גם נכפל, ונאמר: ״יָשֶׁת חֹשֶׁךְ סִתְרוֹ״
sources.says: Maimonides says this image is repeated in 'He made darkness His hiding place'.

18:15.headline: Lightning in plenty, or lightning He shot like arrows?
18:15.body: רב usually means 'much'. Metzudat Zion, Ibn Ezra and Meiri read it as a verb, 'He shot', as in 'he became an archer (רבה קשת)' and 'they shot at him (ורבו)' in Genesis.

sources.quote: רב. ענין השלכת חצים כמו רובה קשת
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means shooting arrows, as in 'an archer'.

sources.quote: ומלת רב פעל עבר מפעלי הכפל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says רב is a past-tense verb.

sources.quote: וברקים רב ר״ל ירה כאלו הם חצים מלשון וימררוהו ורובו
sources.says: Meiri says it means He shot lightning as if it were arrows, from 'they embittered him and shot at him'.

18:17.headline: He drew me out: the verb behind Moses' name
18:17.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion say ימשני means 'pulled me out', as in 'I drew him (משיתהו) out of the water' in Exodus 2:10. That verse explains Moses' name, and here David says God drew him from many waters.

sources.quote: יַמְשֵׁנִי. לְשׁוֹן הוֹצָאָה, כְּמוֹ ״כִּי מִן הַמַּיִם מְשִׁיתִהוּ״
sources.says: Rashi says it means taking out, as in 'for I drew him out of the water'.

sources.quote: ימשני. ענין הוצאה כמו מן המים משיתהו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means taking out, as in 'I drew him from the water'.

18:27.headline: With the crooked you twist: pay him back, or wrestle him down?
18:27.body: Radak says God brings the crooked man's own twisted way back on him. Ibn Ezra links it to נפתולי אלהים, Rachel's 'wrestlings of God': you wrestle with him until you win.

sources.quote: ועם עקש תתפתל: תביא עליו כדרכו הנפתלה
sources.says: Radak says God brings on him the same twisted way he took.

sources.quote: תתפתל - כמו: נפתולי אלהים על דרך תלחם עד שתנצחנו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is like 'wrestlings of God': you fight until you defeat him.

18:30.headline: ארץ גדוד: I crush a troop, or I run at a troop?
18:30.body: Radak and Ibn Ezra read ארץ from רצץ, to crush: with your help I break the enemy troops. Both also give the plain reading, 'I run at a troop'.

sources.quote: כי בך ארץ גדוד בעזרתך אשבר גדודי איבי. וארוץ משרש רצץ
sources.says: Radak says with your help I break the troops of my enemies, and ארץ is from the root רצץ, to crush.

sources.quote: או פרושו: ארץ לקראת גדוד איבי ולא אירא מהם
sources.says: Radak also says it can mean 'I run toward my enemies' troop and do not fear them'.

sources.quote: כי, ארוץ - כמו ארצץ
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is like 'I crush'.

sources.quote: ויש אומרים: ארוץ אחרי הגדוד כדרך ארדוף
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some read 'I run after the troop', like 'I pursue'.

18:30.headline: Leaping over a שור: here the word means a wall
18:30.body: Metzudat Zion says שור here means a wall, as in Genesis 49:22. Rashi tells a midrash: at Jebus, Joab climbed a bent cypress onto the wall, and God lowered the wall so David leaped over.

sources.quote: שור. חומה כמו בנות צעדה עלי שור
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says שור means a wall, as in 'daughters climb over the wall'.

sources.quote: הֵבִיא יוֹאָב בְּרוֹשׁ רַעֲנָן וּכּפָפוֹ, וְנִתְלָה בּוֹ וְעָלָה עַל הַחוֹמָה
sources.says: Rashi says Joab brought a fresh cypress, bent it, hung on it and climbed onto the wall.

sources.quote: קִצֵּר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת הַחוֹמָה וְדִלֵּג
sources.says: Rashi says God made the wall shorter for David, and he leaped over.

18:31.headline: God's word is refined, or it refines people?
18:31.body: Radak reads צרופה as refined like metal, with no dross in it. Maimonides cites a midrash that reads it as refining people: the commandments were given to refine God's creatures, a saying he calls very unusual.

sources.quote: ואמרתו צרופה שאין בכל משפטיו סיג
sources.says: Radak says His word is refined: there is no dross in any of His judgments.

sources.quote: צְרוּפָה. בְּרוּרָה; מַבְטִיחַ וְעוֹשֶׂה
sources.says: Rashi says it means clear: He promises and does.

sources.quote: לא נִתנו המצוות אלא לצרוף בהן את הבריות
sources.says: Maimonides quotes the midrash: the commandments were given only to refine people through them.

sources.quote: אף על פי שהדברים האלה חריגים מאוד, ואין דומה להם בדבריהם
sources.says: Maimonides says these words are very unusual and have no parallel in the sages' sayings.

18:34.headline: Why 'hinds' and not stags? Rashi on the female deer's feet
18:34.body: Rashi stops on the female form and says the feet of female deer stand straighter than the males'. So the verse compares David's footing to the steadiest of the deer.

sources.quote: רַגְלֵי הַנְּקֵבוֹת עוֹמְדוֹת בְּיֹשֶׁר יוֹתֵר מִשֶּׁל זְכָרִים
sources.says: Rashi says the feet of the females stand straighter than those of the males.

18:35.headline: My arms bend a bronze bow, or break it?
18:35.body: Rashi reads ונחתה as bending a bow, from נחת as in 'your arrows have come down (נחתו) on me'. Metzudat Zion and Radak read it as breaking: a bronze bow breaks in David's arms.

sources.quote: וְנִחֲתָה לְשׁוֹן דְּרִיכַת קֶשֶׁת, כְּמוֹ ״חִצֶּיךָ נִחֲתוּ בִי״
sources.says: Rashi says it means drawing a bow, as in 'your arrows have come down on me'.

sources.quote: ונחתה. מלשון תחת ושבר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is a word of breaking.

sources.quote: כל כך למד ידי עד שיפילו קשת נחושה מאיבי, והיתה נשברת בזרועתי
sources.says: Radak says God trained his hands so well that a bronze bow from his enemies would break in his arms.

18:36.headline: Your humility made me great: God's, or the humility God gave me?
18:36.body: Rashi and Radak read it as God's own humility: God lowered Himself, as it were, to care for David. Ibn Ezra reads it as the humility God placed in David, which made him great.

sources.quote: הִרְבֵּיתָה מִדַּת עֲנָוְתְךָ לְהִתְנַהֵג בָּהּ עִמִּי
sources.says: Rashi says God increased His humility in dealing with me.

sources.quote: ואמר: וענותך דרך משל כאלו השפלת כבודך להשגיח בי
sources.says: Radak says it is a figure of speech, as if God lowered His glory to watch over me.

sources.quote: וזאת הענוה ששמת בי היא תגדלני ותעצימני
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the humility God put in me is what makes me great and strong.

18:43.headline: I poured them out, or trod them into muck?
18:43.body: Rashi reads it as thin, poured-out mud, like 'they emptied (מריקים) their sacks', and Metzudat Zion from ריק, empty. Radak and Meiri take it from רקק, marsh mud: I made them into muck like the mud of the streets.

sources.quote: כְּטִיט הַנָּרוּק, שֶׁאֵינוֹ עָב. כְּמוֹ ״הֵם מְרִיקִים שַׂקֵּיהֶם״
sources.says: Rashi says like poured-out mud that is not thick, as in 'they emptied their sacks'.

sources.quote: אריקם. מלשון ריקן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from the word for empty.

sources.quote: ופרושו: אשימם רקק, כמו טיט חוצות
sources.says: Radak says it means I will make them marsh mud, like the mud of the streets.

sources.quote: ר״ל ארמסם כלומ׳ אעשה אותם רקק
sources.says: Meiri says it means I will trample them, making them into mud.

18:45.headline: ישמעו: they obey me, or they gather to me?
18:45.body: Rashi reads it as obeying: they come under my command. Radak and Ibn Ezra read it as gathering, like 'Saul summoned (וישמע) the people', since people gather when a herald calls out.

sources.quote: יִשָּׁמְעוּ לִי. יָסוּרוּ אֶל מִשְׁמַעְתִּי, וְיִהְיוּ נִשְׁמָעִים לִדְבָרַי
sources.says: Rashi says they will come under my command and obey my words.

sources.quote: ופרוש ישמעו: יתקבצו כמו וישמע שאול את העם
sources.says: Radak says ישמעו means they will gather, as in 'Saul summoned the people'.

sources.quote: והוא לשון קבוץ לפי שקבוץ העם על ידי השמעת קול הכרוז
sources.says: Radak says it is a word for gathering, because people gather when the herald's voice is heard.

sources.quote: לשמע, ישמעו - כדרך וישמע שאול יתחברו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means they will join together, as in 'Saul summoned'.

18:46.headline: ויחרגו: tremble, loosen, or limp? A word with no partner
18:46.body: Ibn Ezra says ויחרגו has no partner in Scripture and reads it, as Rashi does, from the Targum's word for terror. Rashi also cites Menachem, who reads it as loosening a belt, and Dunash, who reads it as limping.

sources.quote: ויחרגו - כתרגום: חרגת מותא ואין ריע לו במקרא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is as in the Targum's 'the terror of death', and it has no partner in Scripture.

sources.quote: וְיַחְרְגוּ. לְשׁוֹן אֵימָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word for terror.

sources.quote: מְנַחֵם פָּתַר אוֹתוֹ לְשׁוֹן רִפְיוֹן חֲגוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi says Menachem explained it as loosening a belt.

sources.quote: וְדוּנָ״שׁ פָּתַר וְיַחְרְגוּ מִמִּסְגְּרוֹתֵיהֶם וְיִפְסְחוּ מִכַּבְלֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says Dunash explained it as 'they will limp from their chains'.

18:48.headline: תחתי: beneath me, or in my place?
18:48.body: תחתי usually means 'under me'. Rashi reads it here as 'in my place': nations given as ransom for David, as in 'I give people in your place' in Isaiah 43:4.

sources.quote: תַּחְתָּי. בִּמְקוֹמִי וְחִלּוּפִי, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וָאֶתֵּן אָדָם תַּחְתֶּיךָ״
sources.says: Rashi says it means in my place and as my exchange, as in 'I give people in your place'.

19:2.headline: Who does the telling: the heavens, or the people who see them?
19:2.body: Rashi and Radak say people tell of God's glory when they look at the heavens. Maimonides says the heavens themselves tell it, because Hebrew uses ספור and הגדה together only for beings with a mind.

sources.quote: מִתּוֹךְ כָּךְ מְסַפְּרִים הַבְּרִיּוֹת כְּבוֹד אֵל וּמוֹדִים וּמְבָרְכִין עַל הַמְּאוֹרוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says that because of the lights, people tell of God's glory and give thanks and bless over the lights.

sources.quote: כי מהנפלאות והמעשים הגדולים שאדם רואה בשמים יספר האדם כבוד האל
sources.says: Radak says that from the great wonders a person sees in the heavens, the person tells of God's glory.

sources.quote: זאת משום שהעברית אינה משתמשת בלשון "הגדה" ו"סיפור" יחד אלא על בעלי שכל
sources.says: Maimonides says Hebrew uses the language of הגדה and ספור together only for beings with intellect, so the heavens themselves are telling.

19:3.headline: יביע can mean 'speaks' or 'gushes like a spring'
19:3.body: Radak says יביע means 'speaks', like יביעון בפיהם. Rashi, quoting Menachem, ties it to a flowing spring, and Ibn Ezra adds that it never stops.

sources.quote: יביע ידבר, כמו הנה יביעון בפיהם
sources.says: Radak says יביע means 'speaks', like הנה יביעון בפיהם.

sources.quote: מְנַחֵם פֵּתַר ״יַבִּיעַ״ לְשׁוֹן ״מַעְיָן נוֹבֵעַ״
sources.says: Rashi says Menachem explained יביע as the language of a flowing spring.

sources.quote: יביע - שלא יפסוק כמו מבוע, או כמו יגיד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says יביע means it never stops, like מבוע (a spring), or else it means 'tells'.

19:5.headline: קום, 'their line': a builder's line, or a line of writing?
19:5.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion say קום is the line a builder uses, so it means the heavens' structure. Ibn Ezra says it is a line of writing, which people read everywhere.

sources.quote: קום בנינם; וכן קו לקו (ישעיהו כה יא), לפי שהבנין יעשה בהטית הקו
sources.says: Radak says קום means their structure, like קו לקו, because a building is made by stretching the line.

sources.quote: קום. ר״ל הבנין שלהם הנעשה בנטיית קו המשקל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means their structure, made by stretching the measuring line.

sources.quote: בכל קום - כמו קו לקו והוא המכתב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says קום is like קו לקו and means the writing.

19:7.headline: 'Nothing hides from his heat': why heat, and not light?
19:7.body: Radak says the verse says heat, not light, because a person can hide from light but not from heat. Ibn Ezra says the sun's heat is like the heart's heat in the body, giving life to all.

sources.quote: ואמר: ואין נסתר מחמתו, ולא אמר: ואין נסתר ממאורו, כי יוכל האדם להסתר ממאורו ולא מחמו
sources.says: Radak says the verse says heat and not light, because a person can hide from its light but not from its heat.

sources.quote: כי חמת השמש בעולם כדמות חום הלב בגוף האדם, מראיות חכמת התולדת והנה הוא חיי כל הגופות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the sun's heat in the world is like the heat of the heart in a person's body, and it is the life of all bodies.

19:8.headline: תורה: 'instruction' in how to act, or the whole Book
19:8.body: Ibn Ezra and Radak say תורה means instruction in how a thing is done, like 'the law of the leper'. Radak adds that the whole Five Books are also called תורה.

sources.quote: ופירוש תורה – שתורה הדרך הישרה בסימנים נזכרים כמו תורת הצרעת והנזיר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says תורה means it teaches the right way by stated signs, like the law of the leper and the Nazirite.

sources.quote: והתורה היא תכונת המצוה היאך תעשה
sources.says: Radak says תורה is the form of a commandment: how it is done.

sources.quote: ואף על פי כן הספר נקרא בשם התורה מבראשית עד לעיני כל ישראל
sources.says: Radak adds that the whole book, from Genesis to the end, is still called תורה.

19:8.headline: תמימה, 'complete': whole like the sun, lacking nothing
19:8.body: Radak says תמימה means whole, lacking nothing a person needs. Ibn Ezra says it echoes the sun, whole in its light unlike the moon, and Maimonides cites it for the Torah's balance and wisdom.

sources.quote: תמימה שהיא שלמה כלה, לא יחסר דבר בה מכל הדברים שצריך אדם להם בעולם הזה ובעולם הבא
sources.says: Radak says תמימה means whole and complete, lacking nothing a person needs in this world and the next.

sources.quote: וטעם לאמר תמימה – כנגד השמש, בעבור היות השמש תמימה באורה ואיננה כמו הלבנה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says תמימה is set against the sun, which is whole in its light, unlike the moon.

sources.quote: לכן נאמר עליה: תּוֹרַת ה' תְּמִימָה
sources.says: Maimonides cites 'the Torah of the Lord is perfect' for the balance and wisdom of the commandments.

19:8.headline: משיבת נפש: 'turns the soul back' or 'calms it'
19:8.body: Rashi says it turns a person from the ways of death to the ways of life. Metzudat Zion and Meiri read it as giving rest, ending the toil of doubts.

sources.quote: מְשִׁיבָתוֹ מִדַּרְכֵי מִיתָה לְדַרְכֵי חַיִּים
sources.says: Rashi says it brings a person back from the ways of death to the ways of life.

sources.quote: משיבת. ענין הנחה והשקטה כמו למשיב נפש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says משיבת means setting at rest and quieting, like למשיב נפש.

sources.quote: או ענינו ענין מנוחה כלומ׳ שתניח מעמל המבוכות והספקות
sources.says: Meiri says it may mean rest: it lets a person rest from the toil of confusions and doubts.

19:9.headline: פקודי: 'commandments', or 'deposits' kept in the mind
19:9.body: Radak says the Targum's 'commandments' would repeat מצות, so he reads פקודי as 'deposits', from פקדון: things stored in the mind that reason confirms. Ibn Ezra and Meiri also read it from פקדון.

sources.quote: פקודי מצות כתרגומו, אלא שאמר אחר כן מצות יי', לפיכך נפרש פקודי מגזרת והיה האכל לפקדון
sources.says: Radak says we would read פקודי as 'commandments' like the Targum, but since the verse then says מצות, he reads it from פקדון, a deposit.

sources.quote: פקודי - מגזרת פקדון והמה הנמצאות בכח הנשמה בכל אדם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says פקודי comes from פקדון, and they are what is found in the power of the soul in every person.

sources.quote: ומלת פקודים נגזרת מפקדון שהוא עומד צרור ומונח
sources.says: Meiri says פקודים comes from פקדון, something kept bundled and stored.

19:10.headline: 'Fear of the Lord' stands for a group of commands
19:10.body: Ibn Ezra says יראת ה' means the prohibitions. Radak says it means things done in secret, and Meiri says it means the commandments whose reason is not clear.

sources.quote: יראת - מצות לא תעשה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says יראת means the prohibitions.

sources.quote: והם הדברים שיעשה אדם אותם בסתר, או בלי דעת כמו הגנבה וזיוף המדות והמשקלות
sources.says: Radak says it means the things a person might do in secret or without anyone knowing, like theft and false weights.

sources.quote: הוא חלק המצוות שאין ההקש שלהם ברור כאכילת חזיר ולבישת כלאים ודומיהם
sources.says: Meiri says it is the group of commandments whose reasoning is not clear, like eating pork and wearing mixed fabrics.

19:10.headline: משפטי: laws whose purpose is clear to everyone
19:10.body: Maimonides says laws whose benefit is clear to people are called משפטים, and those whose benefit is not clear are called חקים. Radak says משפטים are the laws between one person and another.

sources.quote: אלה שתועלתן ברורה להמון קרויות "מִשְׁפָּטִים", ואלה שתועלתן אינה ברורה להמון קרויות "חֻקִּים"
sources.says: Maimonides says commandments whose benefit is clear to the crowd are called משפטים, and those whose benefit is not clear are called חקים.

sources.quote: כבר פרשנו המשפטים שהם הדינים שבין אדם לחברו
sources.says: Radak says משפטים are the laws between a person and his fellow.

19:11.headline: פז: fine gold, or precious stones
19:11.body: Radak says פז is good, clean gold. Ibn Ezra says it means precious stones.

sources.quote: ומפז הוא הזהב הטוב הנקי
sources.says: Radak says פז is the good, clean gold.

sources.quote: מתאוים להיות להם זהב ופז רב, הם אבנים יקרות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says פז is precious stones.

19:11.headline: 'Fine gold, רב': is it 'great', or 'much'?
19:11.body: Radak says רב can mean great in worth, like רב ביתו, 'the chief of his house', or else 'much' in number. Meiri also takes it as 'most important of the important'.

sources.quote: רב כמו על כל רב ביתו (אסתר א ח) שהוא גדול בחשיבות ובגדלה. או יהיה פרוש רב במנין
sources.says: Radak says רב is like רב ביתו, great in importance and size, or else it means many in number.

sources.quote: ומפז רב פירושו חשוב שבחשובים כמו על כל רב ביתו
sources.says: Meiri says פז רב means the most important of the important, like רב ביתו.

19:12.headline: עקב means 'heel', 'end', 'reward', or 'because'
19:12.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion say עקב is the reward, the end of the deed, as the heel is the end of the body. Rashi first reads it as 'because', like עקב אשר שמע אברהם, and also as 'end'.

sources.quote: עקב. ענין שכר וגמול שהוא סוף המעשה כהעקב הזה שהוא סוף הגוף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says עקב means reward and payment, which is the end of the deed, like the heel, which is the end of the body.

sources.quote: לפיכך נקרא השכר עקב רב כמו שהעקב הוא סוף הגוף, כן השכר סוף המעשה
sources.says: Radak says the reward is called עקב because the heel is the end of the body and the reward is the end of the deed.

sources.quote: וְלַלָּשׁוֹן הַזֶּה עֵקֶב כְּמוֹ ״עֵקֶב אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַע אַבְרָהָם בְּקוֹלִי״
sources.says: Rashi says this sense of עקב is like עקב אשר שמע אברהם בקולי, 'because Abraham listened to my voice'.

sources.quote: עֵקֶב לְשׁוֹן סוֹף, וְיֵשׁ לוֹ חָבֵר בִּלְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָה: עִקְּבוֹת מְשִׁיחָא
sources.says: Rashi says that in another reading עקב means 'end', with a partner in the language of the Mishnah: עקבות משיחא.

19:14.headline: מזדים: willful sins, or arrogant people?
19:14.body: Rashi, Radak and Meiri read זדים as willful sins (זדונות). Ibn Ezra and the Targum read it as insolent people.

sources.quote: גַּם מִזֵּדִים. מִן הַזְּדוֹנוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says מזדים means from willful sins.

sources.quote: שיחשכהו מחברת הזדים ומרעתם ואל ימשלו בו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means God should hold him back from the company of the זדים and their evil, so they do not rule him.

sources.quote: בְּרַם מִן זֵידָנַיָא פְּצָא עַבְדָךְ
sources.says: The Targum renders it: save your servant from the insolent ones.

19:14.headline: פשע is not just sin: it is open rebellion
19:14.body: Rashi and Meiri say פשעים means rebellions, done to anger God. Radak says פשע is worse than willful sin, since the rebel scorns his master even without wanting the sin.

sources.quote: פְּשָׁעִים אֵלּוּ הַמְּרָדִים, שֶׁמִּתְכַּוֵּן לְהַכְעִיס
sources.says: Rashi says פשעים are rebellions, done in order to anger.

sources.quote: אבל הפשע רב הוא המורד באדוניו, ויבזה מצותיו, ויעשה העברה, אף על פי שאינו מתאוה אליה
sources.says: Radak says פשע is the one who rebels against his master, scorns his commandments, and sins even though he does not desire it.

sources.quote: ופשעים הם המרדים
sources.says: Meiri says פשעים are rebellions.

19:15.headline: הגיון is a silent thought in the heart
19:15.body: Radak and Rashi say הגיון is what a person thinks in the heart without saying it. Metzudat David adds that it covers thoughts he cannot put into words.

sources.quote: והגיון לבי לפניך ומה שלא אמרתי בפי, אלא חשבתי בלבי, והמחשבה הוא הגיון הלב
sources.says: Radak says הגיון לבי is what I did not say with my mouth but thought in my heart; thought is the הגיון of the heart.

sources.quote: כָּל לְשׁוֹן הֶגֶה בַּלֵּב הוּא, כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר ״וְהֶגְיוֹן לִבִּי״
sources.says: Rashi says every use of the root הגה is in the heart, as in והגיון לבי.

sources.quote: גם מחשבות לבי מה שלא אוכל להוציא בפה גם המה יהיו לרצון לפניך
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means the thoughts of my heart that I cannot put into words, which also should be acceptable.

2:2.headline: Secret counsel or laying a foundation
2:2.body: Rashi reads נוסדו from סוד, a secret plan. Radak links it to יסוד, a foundation, because a plan is the base that an action is built on.

sources.quote: נוֹסְדוּ. לְשׁוֹן סוֹד
sources.says: Rashi says נוסדו comes from the word for secret counsel.

sources.quote: ונאמרה העצה בלשון יסוד כי כן העצה למעשה כמו היסוד לבנין
sources.says: Radak says the plan is called by the word for a foundation, because a plan is to an action what a foundation is to a building.

2:4.headline: God sitting in heaven means God never changes
2:4.body: Maimonides says יושב, sitting, is said of God to mean being fixed and unchanging, not a body seated on a chair. Radak agrees that it means God stands firm forever.

sources.quote: "יוֹשֵׁב בַּשָּׁמַיִם" (שם ב,ד) – הקיים לעד והיציב שאינו משתנה באף אופן מאופני השינוי
sources.says: Maimonides says “sitting in heaven” means the One who lasts forever and does not change in any way.

sources.quote: ובאמרו: יושב בשמים ענין יושב עומד, כמו ואתה יי' לעולם תשב
sources.says: Radak says “sitting” here means remaining firm, as in “You, God, sit forever.”

2:12.headline: Kiss, arm yourselves, or long for?
2:12.body: Ibn Ezra reads נשקו as kissing, as people kiss a king. He also reports a reading from נשק, weapons: arm yourselves. Rashi gives the arming reading and Menachem’s reading of longing.

sources.quote: ומנהג גוים בעולם לשום ידיהם תחת יד המלך כאחי שלמה, או העבד תחת ירך אדוניו, או לנשק את המלך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says nations show loyalty by placing their hands under the king’s hand, or by kissing the king.

sources.quote: ויש אומרים: כי נשקו – מגזרת נשק
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports that some take נשקו from the word for weapons.

sources.quote: זָרְזוּ עַצְמְכֶם בְּבַר לֵב. (נוסח אחר) נַשְּׁקוּ בַר. אַרְנִישְׁמְנְט בְּלַעַ״ז, וּמְנַחֵם פָּתַר אוֹתוֹ לְשׁוֹן תַּאֲוָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means equip yourselves with a pure heart, gives the Old French word for armament, and reports that Menachem read it as longing.

21:2.headline: Which king: David, or the Messiah?
21:2.body: The sages read 'the king' in this psalm as the Messiah, and the Targum translates it 'the King Messiah'. Rashi and Meiri say it fits David himself as well.

sources.quote: רַבּוֹתֵינוּ פָּתְרוּהוּ עַל מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ, וְנָכוֹן הַדָּבָר לְפוֹתְרוֹ עוֹד עַל דָּוִד עַצְמוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the sages explained it about the King Messiah, and it is right to explain it also about David himself.

sources.quote: יְיָ בְעָשְׁנָךְ יֶחְדֵי מְלַךְ מְשִׁיחָא
sources.says: The Targum translates it as 'Lord, in your strength the King Messiah will rejoice'.

sources.quote: זה המזמור פירשוהו רז״ל נבואה לעתיד על מלך המשיח
sources.says: Meiri says the sages explained this psalm as a prophecy about the King Messiah, though he thinks it was said about David himself.

21:3.headline: A one-time word for speech, or for the power of a king's word
21:3.body: Rashi and Radak say ארשת means speech and appears nowhere else in the Bible, and Menachem linked it to the 'permission' Cyrus gave in Ezra. The Midrash reads it as the authority in the king's lips: when he decrees, it is done.

sources.quote: וַאֲרֶשֶׁת. לְשׁוֹן דִּבּוּר, וְאֵין לוֹ דִּמְיוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says the word means speech and has no parallel.

sources.quote: וּמְנַחֵם הֵבִיא לוֹ חָבֵר: ״כְּרִשְׁיוֹן כּוֹרֶשׁ מֶלֶךְ פָּרַס״
sources.says: Rashi says Menachem found a related word in 'by the permission of Cyrus king of Persia'.

sources.quote: וארשת שפתיו כמו מבטא שפתי, ואין לו חבר במקרא
sources.says: Radak says it is like 'the utterance of my lips' and has no other example in scripture.

sources.quote: ואין לו דומה במקרא ובפייט של ר״ה ארשת שפתינו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it has no parallel in scripture, and is used in the Rosh Hashanah prayer 'the utterance of our lips'.

sources.quote: ומהו ארשת שפתיו רשות שבשפתיו
sources.says: The Midrash says ארשת means the authority in his lips.

21:4.headline: Blessings of good: of every good thing, of Moses, or of Torah
21:4.body: Radak reads 'blessings of good' as blessings of every good thing. The Midrash has two other readings: the blessings of Moses, whom the Torah calls 'good' at his birth, or the blessings of the Torah, called 'a good teaching'.

sources.quote: ברכות כל דבר טוב
sources.says: Radak says it means blessings of every good thing.

sources.quote: רבי יהודה אומר ברכות משה שנקרא טוב
sources.says: The Midrash quotes Rabbi Yehudah: these are the blessings of Moses, who was called 'good'.

sources.quote: רבנן אמרי ברכותיה של תורה
sources.says: The Midrash says the sages held these are the blessings of the Torah.

21:4.headline: A crown of paz: fine gold, or gold set with jewels
21:4.body: The Targum translates פז as refined gold. Ibn Ezra says the crown was gold with paz, precious stones, set around it, as kings wear, and Rashi ties it to the Ammonite crown placed on David's head.

sources.quote: כְּלִיל דְהַב סְנִינָא
sources.says: The Targum translates it as 'a crown of refined gold'.

sources.quote: עטרת - זהב עם פז אבנים יקרות סביבה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the crown is gold with paz, precious stones, around it.

sources.quote: ״וַיִּקַּח עֲטֶרֶת מַלְכָּם וַתְּהִי עַל רֹאשׁ דָּוִד״
sources.says: Rashi links it to 'he took the crown of their king, and it was placed on David's head'.

21:6.headline: Majesty for the teacher, splendor for the student
21:6.body: The Midrash reads הוד as the majesty of a teacher and הדר as the splendor of a student. It points to Moses, who was told to give Joshua 'some of your majesty', but not all of it.

sources.quote: הוד של רב והדר של תלמיד
sources.says: The Midrash says הוד is the majesty of the teacher and הדר is the splendor of the student.

sources.quote: ונתתה מהודך עליו. מהודך ולא כל הודך
sources.says: The Midrash cites 'put some of your majesty on him' and says: some of your majesty, not all of it.

21:9.headline: 'Your hand will find': will be enough, or will catch
21:9.body: The verse says תמצא twice. Meiri says the first means 'will be enough', so the king needs no other help, and the second means really finding the enemies, so they cannot run away.

sources.quote: תמצא ידך ר״ל תספיק ידך לכל איביך ולא אצטרך לעזר אחרים
sources.says: Meiri says 'your hand will find' means your hand will be enough against all your enemies, with no need for others' help.

sources.quote: ימינך תמצא שנאיך הוא ענין מציאה ממש כלומ׳ שלא יוכלו לברוח
sources.says: Meiri says 'your right hand will find your haters' means actual finding, so they cannot escape.

sources.quote: תמצא. תספיק כמו ומצא להם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means 'will be enough', as in 'would it suffice for them' in Numbers.

21:10.headline: Like a fiery oven: burning others, or burned inside it
21:10.body: Radak and Meiri say the enemies do not become an oven that burns others; they are like the wood inside the oven, burned up. Ibn Ezra cites a reading of 'like an oven' as 'in an oven'.

sources.quote: שאינו אומר שהם יהיו אש לבער אחרים, אלא שיהיו כאש שתצא ביער שיכלו
sources.says: Radak says the verse does not mean they become a fire that burns others, but that they are consumed, like a forest in a fire.

sources.quote: ולא שיהיו הם כתנור אש לכלות האחרים אבל שיהיו כאלו הם בתוך תנור אש
sources.says: Meiri says it does not mean they become a fiery oven that destroys others, but that they are as if inside a fiery oven.

sources.quote: ויש אומרים: כי כ"ף כתנור אש כמו בי"ת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some read the letter כ in 'like an oven' as ב, 'in an oven'.

21:13.headline: Shekhem: a shoulder, or a share
21:13.body: שכם means a shoulder, but Metzudat Zion says here it means a portion. Rashi says the enemies become a share whose wealth Israel divides, while Radak says God gathers them all on one side, facing him.

sources.quote: שכם. חלק כמו שכם אחד
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a portion, as in 'one portion' that Jacob gave Joseph.

sources.quote: אֲשֶׁר תָּשִׁית אוֹתָם לְחֵלֶק, שֶׁיְּחַלְּקוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת מָמוֹנָם
sources.says: Rashi says God will make them a share, so that Israel will divide their wealth.

sources.quote: כי אתה תשים אותם לחלק אחד כלם
sources.says: Radak says God will put them all together into one group.

sources.quote: מְטוּל דְשַׁוִיתִנוּן לְעַמָךְ כְּתַף חַד
sources.says: The Targum translates it as 'you will make them one shoulder for your people'.

21:13.headline: Your cords: bowstrings, or tent ropes
21:13.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion say מיתריך are the strings of God's bows, ready to shoot arrows at the enemy. The Targum reads them as the ropes of God's tabernacle.

sources.quote: בְּמֵיתְרֵי קַשְּׁתוֹתֶיךָ תְּכוֹנֵן חִצֶּיךָ
sources.says: Rashi says God will set his arrows on the strings of his bows.

sources.quote: במיתריך. הוא חבל הקשת כמו על יתר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the bowstring, as in 'on the string'.

sources.quote: בְּאַטוּנֵי מַשְׁכְּנָךְ
sources.says: The Targum translates it as 'with the ropes of your tabernacle'.

22:1.headline: Dawn light comes slowly, and so does rescue
22:1.body: Rashi reads השחר as 'the dawn', though Menachem took it from a word for seeking. In the Midrash, two rabbis watch the dawn break and say Israel's rescue comes the same way, little by little.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן שַׁחֲרִית, וּמְנַחֵם פָּתַר לְשׁוֹן בִּקּוּר
sources.says: Rashi says השחר means morning, while Menachem read it as seeking.

sources.quote: וראו אילת השחר שבקעה אורה לעלות. אמר לו ר' חייא כך היא גאולתן של ישראל. אמר ליה היינו דכתיב (מיכה ז ח) כי אשב בחשך ה' אור לי. בתחלה היא באה קימעא קימעא
sources.says: The Midrash says Rabbi Chiya saw the dawn break and said Israel's redemption is like it, coming little by little.

22:4.headline: God 'sitting' means God lasts and never changes
22:4.body: יושב usually means sitting. Radak reads it here as lasting forever, as in 'You, LORD, sit forever'. Maimonides says this is what sitting means whenever it is said of God.

sources.quote: יושב: קים נצח, וכן אתה יי' לעולם תשב (איכה ה יט)
sources.says: Radak says יושב here means existing forever, and cites 'You, LORD, sit forever.'

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 1, Chapter 11
sources.quote: הקיים לעד והיציב שאינו משתנה באף אופן מאופני השינוי
sources.says: Maimonides says that sitting, said of God, means He lasts forever and does not change in any way.

22:8.headline: Mockers open their lips, as a firstborn opens the womb
22:8.body: יפטירו is rare. Rashi reads it as 'they open', from פטר רחם, the firstborn who opens the womb. Radak reads it as letting words out, the way water is let out.

sources.quote: יִפְתְּחוּ, כְּמוֹ פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם וּפֶטֶר חֲמוֹר
sources.says: Rashi says יפטירו means 'they open', like the firstborn that opens the womb.

sources.quote: יפטירו: ישלחו הדברים בשפה, מן פוטר מים (משלי יז יד)
sources.says: Radak says it means they send words out with their lips, like one who lets water out.

22:9.headline: Who delights in whom: God in him, or he in God?
22:9.body: כי חפץ בו can mean God delights in the person, or the person delights in God. Radak gives both. Ibn Ezra says only the first is right.

sources.quote: כי חפץ יי' בו ושמע תפלתו. כמו אם חפץ בנו יי' (במדבר יד ח). או פרושו: כי חפץ האדם באל
sources.says: Radak gives both readings: God delights in him and hears his prayer, or the person delights in God.

sources.quote: השם כי טעה האומר, כי הגולל חפץ בשם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is God who delights, and whoever says the person delights in God is wrong.

22:12.headline: Far and near, set side by side
22:12.body: David asks God not to be far, because trouble is near. Ibn Ezra says pairing 'far' with 'near' is a deliberate poetic touch. Radak adds that if God comes near, the trouble will be far.

sources.quote: דרך צחות בשירים תרחק עם קרובה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says putting תרחק, 'be far', next to קרובה, 'near', is a poetic play.

sources.quote: כי צרה קרובה ואם תקרב תהיה רחוקה
sources.says: Radak says the trouble is near, but if God comes near it will be far.

22:13.headline: Enemies ring him round like a crown
22:13.body: כתרוני comes from כתר, a crown. Rashi says the enemies surround him the way a crown goes around the head.

sources.quote: סְבָבוּנִי כְּכֶתֶר הַמַּקֶּפֶת אֶת הָרֹאשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says they surrounded him like a crown that goes around the head.

sources.quote: מן כתר מלכות שהוא עגול
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word comes from the royal crown, which is round.

22:16.headline: Set down in the dust like a pot on the stove
22:16.body: תשפתני is the word for setting a pot on the fire. Rashi reads it as God setting him down in the dust of death. A Midrash pictures a stove at a crossroads that every passerby uses.

sources.quote: אַתָּה תּוֹשִׁיבֵנִי, לְשׁוֹן שְׁפִיתַת קְדֵרָה, ״שְׁפֹת הַסִּיר״
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'you set me down', the word for setting a pot on the fire.

sources.quote: אני דומה לכירה שנתונה בין שתי דרכים ועוברים ושבים שופתים עליה
sources.says: Radak cites a Midrash: I am like a stove between two roads, where every passerby sets his pot.

22:18.headline: Counting my bones, or telling my case?
22:18.body: אספר can mean 'I count' or 'I tell'. Some read that he is so thin he can count his bones. Others read עצמותי as 'my arguments', which he tells to his enemies' leaders.

sources.quote: ויש מפרשים עצמותי כמשמעו מן עצם ויפרשו אספר מענין מספר; ופרושו: מרוב כחישותי אוכל לספר כל עצמותי
sources.says: Radak says some read it as counting: he is so thin he can count all his bones.

sources.quote: י״מ כמו עצומותי כלומ׳ כשאני מספר עצומותי וטענותי לגדוליהם
sources.says: Meiri reports a reading of עצמותי as 'my arguments', which he tells to their leaders.

22:20.headline: 'My strength', a word that echoes the psalm's title
22:20.body: אילותי appears only here and means 'my strength'. Menachem read the title's אילת, 'doe', from this same word, as strength.

sources.quote: כֹּחִי, כְּמוֹ ״הָיִיתִי כְּגֶבֶר אֵין אַיָּל״
sources.says: Rashi says אילותי means 'my strength', like 'a man with no strength'.

sources.quote: וּמְנַחֵם פָּתַר אַיֶּלֶת – לְשׁוֹן מָעוֹז, כְּמוֹ אֱיָלוּתִי לְעֶזְרָתִי חוּשָׁה
sources.says: Rashi reports that Menachem read the title's אילת as strength, like אילותי in this verse.

22:22.headline: 'You answered me', the reply to 'You do not answer'
22:22.body: עניתני is past tense, 'you answered me'. Radak reads it as a plea, 'answer me', or as a memory of past rescues. Ibn Ezra says it answers verse 3: 'I call by day and You do not answer.'

sources.quote: ועניתני כמו תענני ורבים כמוהו בדברי נבואה. או פרושו: כי פעמים רבות הושעתני
sources.says: Radak says עניתני may stand for 'answer me', or recall the many times God already saved him.

sources.quote: וטעם עניתני – כנגד אקרא יומם ולא תענה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says עניתני is set against verse 3, 'I call by day and You do not answer.'

22:30.headline: The fat of the land: food for the humble, or the rich?
22:30.body: דשני ארץ means 'the fat ones of the earth'. Rashi reads it as the land's best food, which the humble will eat. Ibn Ezra reads it as people who live on rich food in this world.

sources.quote: אָכְלוּ עֲנָוִים כָּל דִּשְׁנֵי אֶרֶץ וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ לַה׳ בְּהַלֵּל וְהוֹדָאָה עַל הַטּוֹבָה, דִּשְׁנֵי אֶרֶץ טוּב חֵלֶב הָאָרֶץ
sources.says: Rashi says the humble will eat the best of the land and bow in thanks.

sources.quote: כי דשני ארץ הם המתענגים בעולם הזה לאכול כל דשן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says דשני ארץ are those who enjoy rich food in this world.

23:1.headline: The song comes before the inspiration
23:1.body: Rashi reads מזמור לדוד, “a psalm of David,” as music that brings David divine inspiration. Reversing the words to לדוד מזמור means the inspiration came first.

sources.quote: מִזְמוֹר לְדָוִד. אָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ : כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״מִזְמוֹר לְדָוִד״, מְנַגֵּן וְאַחַר כָּךְ שׁוֹרָה עָלָיו שְׁכִינָה. מִזְמוֹר, לְהָבִיא רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ לְדָוִד. וְכָל שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ ״לְדָוִד מִזְמוֹר״, שָׁרְתָה עָלָיו שְׁכִינָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר שִׁירָה:
sources.says: Rashi says “a psalm of David” puts music before divine inspiration, while “of David, a psalm” reverses the order.

23:3.headline: Restoring strength or giving rest
23:3.body: Rashi reads ישובב as restoring a spirit weakened by trouble and flight. Radak connects it with rest, picturing a shepherd who leads gently and does not exhaust the sheep.

sources.quote: נַפְשִׁי יְשׁוֹבֵב. רוּחִי, שֶׁהוּפַג בַּצָּרוֹת וּבַמְּנוּסָה, יְשׁוֹבֵב לְקַדְמוּתוֹ:
sources.says: Rashi says God restores David’s spirit after distress and flight have weakened it.

sources.quote: נפשי ישובב יניח כמו הרועה הטוב שלא ייגע הצאן ולא ידחפן אלא ינהלן לאט כמו (ישעיהו מ יא): בזרעו יקבץ טלאים ובחיקו ישא עלות ינהל. וישובב מענין בשובה ונחת (שם ל טו).
sources.says: Radak reads ישובב as giving rest and compares a shepherd who guides the flock gently.

23:4.headline: The comforting rod can also mean painful discipline
23:4.body: Radak reads שבטך as the shepherd’s staff that guides the flock. Rashi reads it as suffering that comforts David because it helps bring forgiveness.

sources.quote: שבטך ומשענתך כי הרועה ינהל הצאן במטה אשר בידו וישען עליו כשיעמוד; ואמר:
sources.says: Radak explains the rod and staff as the shepherd’s stick for guiding the flock and leaning on.

sources.quote: שִׁבְטְךָ וּמִשְׁעַנְתֶּךָ. יִסּוּרִים שֶׁבָּאוּ עָלַי וּמִשְׁעָן שֶׁאֲנִי בָּטוּחַ עַל חַסְדְּךָ, שְׁנֵיהֶם יְנַחֲמוּנִי – שֶׁיִּהְיוּ לִי לִסְלֹחַ עָוֹן;
sources.says: Rashi explains the rod as suffering and says it brings comfort through forgiveness.

23:5.headline: The oil can point to a feast or a crown
23:5.body: Ibn Ezra reads דשנת as an image of rich food, as though the head were soaked in fresh oil. Rashi reads the oil as David’s anointing as king.

sources.quote: ומרוב דשן, המטעמים שהם על השלחן ראשו מדושן, כאילו הוא בלול בשמן רענן.
sources.says: Ibn Ezra explains the oil-soaked head through the rich foods on the table.

sources.quote: דִּשַּׁנְתָּ בַשֶּׁמֶן רֹאשִׁי. כְּבָר נִמְשַׁחְתִּי עַל פִּיךָ לְמֶלֶךְ:
sources.says: Rashi says David has already been anointed king at God’s command.

23:6.headline: Goodness becomes a habit that follows him
23:6.body: Ibn Ezra reads ירדפוני, “will pursue me,” as a habit of doing good that becomes hard to leave behind. Even if David tried to stop for a moment, goodness would pursue him.

sources.quote: טוב לנפשי, וחסד עם אחרים ללמדם ולהורותם לעבוד את ה', עד שיהיה לי חוק, כי אילו רציתי להניח הטוב רגע אחד, הוא היה רודף אחרי.
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says doing good becomes so habitual that it would pursue him if he tried to leave it.

24:5.headline: He did not lift a false oath, so he lifts a blessing
24:5.body: The same verb נשא appears in both verses. In verse 4 it means to swear: he did not 'lift' God's name falsely. Here it means to receive: he will 'lift' a blessing. Ibn Ezra says the two are set against each other.

sources.quote: ישא ברכה כנגד: לא נשא לשוא נפשי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'he will lift a blessing' answers 'he did not lift My soul in vain'.

sources.quote: ישא. יקח כמו וישאו להם נשים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ישא here means 'take', as in Ruth 1:4 where men took wives.

24:10.headline: Lord of hosts: the armies of heaven, or of Israel?
24:10.body: Ibn Ezra says the 'hosts' are the hosts of heaven, and he rejects the view that they are Israel's armies. Radak says God is called this here because all of Israel's hosts came to this one Temple.

sources.quote: בעבור צבא השמים כאשר פירשתי, לא בעבור צבא ישראל כאשר אמר הגאון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says God is called this for the hosts of heaven, not for Israel's armies as the Gaon said.

sources.quote: ואמר יי' צבאות לפי שכל צבאות ישראל היו באים בזה הבית
sources.says: Radak says it says 'LORD of hosts' because all of Israel's hosts came to this house to offer sacrifices.

25:2.headline: 'In You' is also the number 22, the alphabet's letters
25:2.body: This psalm runs through the Hebrew alphabet but has no verse for ב. Ibn Ezra suggests the word בך fills that gap. The Midrash reads בך as the number 22: 'in You', that is, in Your Torah written with 22 letters.

sources.quote: אמר רבי יצחק ב"ך בתורתך בעשרים ושתים אותיות
sources.says: Rabbi Yitzchak reads בך as 'in Your Torah, in twenty-two letters'.

sources.quote: יתכן להיות בי"ת בך בטחתי תחת הבי"ת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the ב of בך may stand in for the missing ב line of the alphabet.

25:5.headline: 'All the day': all my life, or this world's long night?
25:5.body: Radak reads כל היום as 'all my days'. Rashi reads 'the day' as this whole world, which is daytime for the nations and night for Israel. David keeps hoping all through it.

sources.quote: הוּא הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁהוּא יוֹם לָאֻמּוֹת וְלַיְלָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Rashi says 'the day' is this world, which is day for the nations and night for Israel.

sources.quote: ופרוש קויתי כל היום: כמו כל הימים
sources.says: Radak says 'all the day' means all the days.

27:1.headline: The sages read "my light" as the New Year
27:1.body: In plain terms the light is rescue from dark times. The midrash reads "my light" as Rosh Hashanah and "my rescue" as Yom Kippur.

sources.quote: רבנן פתרי קראי בראש השנה ויום הכפורים. אורי בראש השנה. וישעי ביום הכפורים
sources.says: The midrash says the rabbis explain these verses about Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur: "my light" is Rosh Hashanah, "my rescue" is Yom Kippur.

sources.quote: כי הצרה דומה לחשכה והתשועה ממנה היא האורה
sources.says: Radak says trouble is like darkness, and rescue from it is the light.

27:2.headline: Coming near, or coming to make war
27:2.body: בקרב can mean "when they come near". It can also come from קרב, battle, so the evildoers are not just close but attacking.

sources.quote: יש מפרשים בקרב מענין קרב ומלחמה, כלומר: בהלחם עלי; או פרושו כמשמעו
sources.says: Radak gives both readings: "when they fight me", from the word for battle, or simply "when they come near".

sources.quote: בקרוב מגזרת: המלמד ידי לקרב. ואחרים אמרו: באשר יקרבו אלי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports one view linking it to "who trains my hands for battle", and another reading it as "when they come near me".

27:3.headline: "In this I trust": in what?
27:3.body: The verse says "in this I trust" but does not say what "this" is. Rashi points back to verse 1, Ibn Ezra mentions a view pointing ahead to verse 4, and the midrash says it is the Torah.

sources.quote: בְּמַה שֶׁאָמַר לְמַעְלָה ה׳ מָעוֹז חַיַּי
sources.says: Rashi says "this" is what he said above: God is the stronghold of my life.

sources.quote: כי בזאת – היא השאלה הנזכרת אחר כן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites a view that "this" is the one request named right after, in verse 4.

sources.quote: בזאת אני בוטח. ואין זאת אלא תורה
sources.says: The midrash says "this" means nothing but the Torah, as in "this is the Torah".

27:4.headline: To visit every morning, or to study closely
27:4.body: ולבקר can come from בקר, morning: to come to God's house every morning. Or it can mean to examine, as when the Torah says a man may not "inspect" good from bad.

sources.quote: וּמְנַחֵם חִבְּרוֹ עִם ״לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין טוֹב לָרָע״ (ויקרא כז:לג), אֲבָל דּוֹנָשׁ פָּתַר לְשׁוֹן בֹּקֶר
sources.says: Rashi says Dunash read it as "morning", to appear there every morning, while Menachem linked it to "he shall not inspect between good and bad".

sources.quote: ללכת בכל בקר ובקר בהיכל השם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites a view that it means to go to God's temple every morning.

sources.quote: ולבקר. ולדרוש כמו לא יבקר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion reads it as "to inquire", like "he shall not inspect".

27:8.headline: "To You" may mean "on Your behalf"
27:8.body: לך looks like "to You". Rashi and Ibn Ezra read it as "for You" or "in Your place": the heart speaks for God and tells the people to seek Him.

sources.quote: בִּמְקוֹמְךָ בָּא אֵלַי לִבִּי לוֹמַר כֵּן
sources.says: Rashi says it means "in Your place": my heart came to me in Your place to say this.

sources.quote: כי לך בעבורך כמו אמרי לי אחי הוא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites Rabbi Moshe that לך means "for Your sake", as in "say of me, he is my brother".

27:11.headline: Enemies who watch with an evil eye
27:11.body: שוררי is a rare word. Metzudat Zion says it means gazing, and Radak explains it as foes who watch him with an evil eye. The Aramaic Targum renders it differently, as "my praises".

sources.quote: ענין הבטה וכן שאפו שוררי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means looking, and explains it as enemies who look at him with an evil eye.

sources.quote: הם האיבים המביטים אותו בעין רעה
sources.says: Radak says these are the enemies who look at him with an evil eye.

sources.quote: מְטוּל תּוּשְׁבְּחָתַי
sources.says: The Targum translates the phrase as "because of my praises".

27:12.headline: Here נפש means will, not soul
27:12.body: נפש usually means soul or life. Maimonides and Radak say that here it means desire: do not hand me over to what my foes want.

sources.quote: וכמוהו: "וְאַל תִּתְּנֵהוּ בְּנֶפֶשׁ צָרָיו" (שילוב של תהילים כז,יב; מא,ג), כלומר אל תסגירהו אל רצונם
sources.says: Maimonides lists נפש as a word with several senses, one being will, and cites this verse to mean "do not hand him over to their will".

sources.quote: אל תתנני בנפש צרי ברצון איבי ותאותם
sources.says: Radak explains it as the will and desire of my enemies.

27:13.headline: Dots over "were it not" mark David's doubt
27:13.body: In the scroll, dots are written over לולא. Rashi and Radak cite the Talmud: David trusted that the righteous are rewarded, but was not sure he had a share.

sources.quote: לוּלֵא נָקוּד עָלָיו, לְמִדְרָשׁ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ
sources.says: Rashi says the word is dotted for a teaching: David knew God rewards the righteous but did not know if he had a share with them.

sources.quote: למה נקוד על לולא
sources.says: Radak quotes the Talmud asking why לולא is dotted, and gives the same answer: perhaps sin would cost him his share.

27:13.headline: "Land of the living": this world or the next?
27:13.body: Radak, Meiri and the Targum read "the land of the living" as the world to come. Metzudat Zion reads it as this world.

sources.quote: וקרא לעולם הבא ארץ חיים
sources.says: Radak says the world to come is called the land of the living, as a figure of speech.

sources.quote: זה העולם נקרא ארץ חיים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says this world is called the land of the living.

sources.quote: והאמנתי לראות בטוב ה׳ בארץ חיים ר״ל העולם הבא
sources.says: Meiri says the land of the living means the world to come.

sources.quote: בְּאַרְעָא דְחַיֵי עַלְמָא
sources.says: The Targum renders it "the land of eternal life".

28:1.headline: תחרש: be silent, or act deaf?
28:1.body: Radak and Meiri say תחרש means silence of a deaf man (חרש): one who ignores a speaker acts as if he cannot hear. Ibn Ezra notes the same root in 'do not plot (תחרש) harm against your neighbor'.

sources.quote: ומלת תחרש כמו תשתוק, כלומר: שתעשה עצמך כחרש שלא תשמע ולא תענני בתפלתי
sources.says: Radak says תחרש means be silent: that you make yourself like a deaf man who does not hear and does not answer my prayer.

sources.quote: תכלית הענין הוא חרש כי השותק לדברי המדבר אליו הוא עושה עצמו כאלו אינו שומע
sources.says: Meiri says the root idea is deafness, because one who is silent to the words of a speaker makes himself as if he does not hear.

sources.quote: ומלת תחרש - מגזרת דומיה ואמרו: אל תחרש על רעך רעה להפריש בינות הטעמים, כי השרש הוא אחד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says תחרש comes from silence, and the root is the same one as in אל תחרש על רעך רעה.

28:3.headline: אל תמשכני: don't draw me into their ways, or their death?
28:3.body: Rashi reads 'do not draw me' as 'do not get me used to' the wicked. Radak reads it as 'do not drag me to die their death', as in Job 21:33.

sources.quote: אַל תַּמְשְׁכֵנִי. אַל תַּרְגִּילֵנִי עִם רְשָׁעִים
sources.says: Rashi says 'do not draw me' means do not accustom me to be with the wicked.

sources.quote: אל תמשכני עם רשעים ועם פעלי און שלא אמות מות רשעים
sources.says: Radak says it means: so that I do not die the death of the wicked.

sources.quote: ואחריו כל אדם ימשוך (איוב כא לג), שפרושו: ימשוך אל המיתה
sources.says: Radak says the same word is in 'and after him every man is drawn', which means drawn to death.

28:5.headline: פעלת ה': God's works in nature, in stories, or in Torah?
28:5.body: Radak says the wicked do not study nature, the heavens and earth God made. The Midrash says the seasons, the stories (הגדות), or the morning blessing 'who forms light', and the Targum says the Torah.

sources.quote: והיא להבין בחכמת הטבע ובפעלותיו ומעשה ידיו בשמים ובארץ
sources.says: Radak says this means understanding the wisdom of nature and God's works in heaven and earth.

sources.quote: חזקיה אמר אלו התקופות. רבי יהושע אומר אלו ההגדות. ורבנן אמרו זו קריאת שמע שהן קורין יוצר אור
sources.says: The Midrash says Chizkiyah held these are the seasons, Rabbi Yehoshua held they are the aggadot, and the Rabbis said it is the Shema with its blessing 'who forms light'.

sources.quote: דְלָא מִתְבַּיְנִין לְאוֹרַיְיתָא דַייָ
sources.says: The Targum renders it: they do not understand the Torah of God.

28:7.headline: ומשירי: with my song, or more than this song?
28:7.body: Ibn Ezra reads the מ as 'with': I will thank Him with my song. Rabbi Moshe HaKohen, whom he quotes, reads it as 'more than': I will thank Him beyond this song.

sources.quote: ומשירי - כמו בשירי הפך והנותר בבשר ובלחם. ואמר רבי משה הכהן: יותר מזה השיר אהודנו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says ומשירי means 'with my song', and Rabbi Moshe HaKohen said it means 'more than this song I will thank Him'.

sources.quote: אודה לו בשיר מן השירים שאמרתי
sources.says: Metzudat David says I will thank Him with one of the songs I have said.

28:9.headline: ונשאם: lift them out of reach, or provide for them?
28:9.body: Ibn Ezra pictures a shepherd keeping his flock on high ground, where wild beasts cannot harm them. Rabbi Moshe, whom he quotes, reads it as 'supply their needs', and Radak reads it as 'raise them above the nations'.

sources.quote: ורעם ונשאם, כלומר שיושבים במקום גבוה שלא תוכלנה החיות להזיקם. ורבי משה אמר: כי ונשאם שיתן להם צרכם כדרך ינשאוהו אנשי מקומו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means they sit in a high place where beasts cannot harm them, and Rabbi Moshe said it means God will give them their needs, as in ינשאוהו אנשי מקומו.

sources.quote: ונשאם על העמים
sources.says: Radak says it means raise them above the nations.

29:1.headline: Who are the 'sons of the mighty': angels, stars, or Israel?
29:1.body: Metzudat David and the Targum say the בני אלים are angels, and Ibn Ezra says they are the stars. Radak says they are Israel, the children of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

sources.quote: בני אלים. הם המלאכים
sources.says: Metzudat David says the sons of the mighty are the angels.

sources.quote: כַתֵּי מַלְאֲכַיָא
sources.says: The Targum translates: bands of angels.

sources.quote: ובני אלים – הם הכוכבים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they are the stars, citing Job 38:7.

sources.quote: ובני אלים הם ישראל שהם בני אברהם יצחק ויעקב
sources.says: Radak says that in his view they are Israel, the children of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

29:2.headline: Bow 'in holy splendor': in the Temple, or with honor?
29:2.body: הדרה is a rare word for splendor. Metzudat David says it means the Temple, the place made splendid by holiness, while Radak reads it as the honor and holiness we give God in words.

sources.quote: במקום שהוא מהודר בקדושה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means the place made splendid by holiness, the Temple.

sources.quote: שתתנו לו בדבריכם הכבוד והקדשה
sources.says: Radak says it means giving God honor and holiness in your words, since splendor here means honor.

29:4.headline: God's voice 'with power', or as strong as people can bear?
29:4.body: Metzudat David reads בכח as 'with great force'. Rashi reads it as 'according to the strength' of the listeners: at Sinai God made His voice only as strong as Israel could bear.

sources.quote: ישאג בכח רב
sources.says: Metzudat David says the voice roars with great force.

sources.quote: צִמְצֵם אֶת קוֹלוֹ לְפִי כֹּחָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Rashi says that at the giving of the Torah God held back His voice to match Israel's strength.

29:7.headline: Hewing flames: lightning, or the Ten Commandments carved in fire?
29:7.body: חצב means to cut stone. Ibn Ezra says the flames are lightning, while Rashi brings the sages: the words of the Ten Commandments came out as flames and were carved on the tablets.

sources.quote: ולפי דעתי: שהטעם על הברקים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says in his view the verse speaks of lightning.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיָה הַדִּבּוּר שֶׁל עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת יוֹצֵא בְּלַהֲבוֹת אֵשׁ מִפִּיו
sources.says: Rashi brings the sages: the speech of the Ten Commandments came out in flames of fire and was carved on the tablets.

29:9.headline: The hinds: real deer giving birth, or nations brought low?
29:9.body: Ibn Ezra says the thunder brings deer into labor, which is hard for them. Rashi reads the hinds as the nations, who now stand firm like a deer's sure feet, and whom God will make tremble.

sources.quote: והזכיר אילות – כי לידתו קשה והנה הרעם מחוללם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says hinds are named because their birth is hard, and the thunder brings on their labor.

sources.quote: שֶׁהֵם עַכְשָׁיו עוֹמְדִים בְּחוֹזֶק כְּאַיָּלוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says God will frighten the idol worshippers, who now stand strong like hinds.

29:9.headline: Stripping the forest: peeling bark, or laying it bare?
29:9.body: Rashi links ויחשף to Genesis 30:37, peeling bark to show the white, and reads it as stripping the proud of their glory. Ibn Ezra says the forest is laid bare when its trees fall.

sources.quote: יְקַלֵּף עֲצֵי הַיַּעַר
sources.says: Rashi says God will peel the trees of the forest, meaning strip the mighty of their glory.

sources.quote: וטעם: ויחשף יערות – יגלה בנפול האילנות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the forest is uncovered when the trees fall.

29:10.headline: God 'sat' at the Flood: He stayed steady while the world changed
29:10.body: ישב means to sit, but Maimonides says that for God it means to stay steady and unchanging. Even when the Flood destroyed the earth, nothing changed in God.

sources.quote: הושאל המונח לכל מצב יציב וקבוע שאינו משתנה
sources.says: Maimonides says sitting first meant the body's sitting, and was then borrowed for anything fixed that does not change.

sources.quote: שגם כאשר מצבי הארץ משתנים ונהרסים, אין אצלו יתעלה שינוי יחס
sources.says: Maimonides says this verse means that even when the earth changes and is destroyed, God's relation to it does not change.

sources.quote: יְתִיב עַל כּוּרְסֵי דְדִינָא
sources.says: The Targum says that at the Flood God sat on the throne of judgment.

29:11.headline: The strength God gives His people is the Torah
29:11.body: עז means strength, as Metzudat David reads it. The Targum translates it as Torah, and Radak brings the sages: 'strength' here means only Torah.

sources.quote: אז יתן ה׳ החוזק לעמו
sources.says: Metzudat David says God will then give His people strength.

sources.quote: יְיָ אוֹרַיְתָא לְעַמֵיהּ יְהַב
sources.says: The Targum translates: the LORD gave the Torah to His people.

sources.quote: ואין עוז אלא תורה
sources.says: Radak brings the sages' reading that 'strength' here means only Torah.

30:2.headline: You lifted me up, so I will lift you up
30:2.body: דליתני means 'you lifted me up,' and Radak pictures David pulled up out of a pit of sin. Ibn Ezra says the opening words 'I will lift you up' are set against it.

sources.quote: רוממתני כמו דלו עיני למרום
sources.says: Metzudat Zion explains it as 'you raised me' and compares 'my eyes are lifted on high' in Isaiah 38:14.

sources.quote: שטבעתי בבור החטא ואתה העליתני ממנו
sources.says: Radak says David had sunk in the pit of sin and God brought him up out of it.

sources.quote: ארוממך - כנגד דליתני
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'I will lift you up' answers 'you lifted me.'

30:3.headline: Healed from sickness, or forgiven for sin?
30:3.body: Rashi says the healing here is forgiveness, as in Isaiah's 'he will repent and be healed.' Ibn Ezra reads a real illness: David was sick, and he cried to God alone, not to a doctor.

sources.quote: הִיא סְלִיחַת עָוֹן, כְּמוֹ ״וְשָׁב וְרָפָא לוֹ״
sources.says: Rashi says the healing means forgiveness of sin.

sources.quote: שועתי אליך - לבדך ולא לרופא ותרפאני
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says David called to God alone and not to a doctor.

sources.quote: ואותו הזמן חלה דוד ויחי מחליו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says David was sick at that time and recovered.

30:8.headline: What is the mountain God made strong?
30:8.body: Rashi reads הררי, 'my mountain,' as David's greatness, and Radak reads it as his mind. Ibn Ezra reports another reading: God set David up like a mountain.

sources.quote: בִּרְצוֹנוֹ הֶעֱמִיד אֶת הֲרָרִי, אֶת גְּדֻלָּתִי, לִהְיוֹת עֹז
sources.says: Rashi says 'my mountain' is David's greatness, which God made strong.

sources.quote: להררי פרושו: לשכלי, שהיה הררי
sources.says: Radak says the mountain is David's mind.

sources.quote: ואחרים אמרו: כי יו"ד להררי סימן המדבר, והטעם לשום אותו כמו הר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports a reading where the last letter means 'me,' so God set David up like a mountain.

30:10.headline: Is it my spilled blood, or my life itself?
30:10.body: Metzudat David reads בדמי plainly: what use is my blood once it is spilled? Radak and Meiri read 'my blood' as 'my life,' because, as Radak puts it, the blood is the life.

sources.quote: מה תועלת כשישפך דמי
sources.says: Metzudat David asks what use there is when David's blood is spilled.

sources.quote: בדמי הוא נפשי כי הדם הוא הנפש
sources.says: Radak says 'my blood' means my life, because blood is the life.

sources.quote: כי מה בצע בדמי ר״ל בנפשי
sources.says: Meiri says 'in my blood' means 'in my life.'

31:5.headline: תוציאני: asking to leave a net he is not in
31:5.body: David was not caught in the net, yet he asks to be taken out of it. Radak and Meiri say he speaks by what his enemies think: in their minds they have already caught him.

sources.quote: והנה הוא לא נלכד ברשתם שטמנו לו; אלא אמר: תוציאני לפי מחשבתם שהם חושבים
sources.says: Radak says David was not caught in the net they hid for him, but he said 'take me out' according to what they think.

sources.quote: אמ׳ תוציאני, אע״פ שהוא לא נלכד ברשתם, מצד מחשבתם
sources.says: Meiri says he said 'take me out' even though he was not caught in their net, because of their thoughts.

31:6.headline: אפקיד רוחי: leaving my spirit with God as a deposit
31:6.body: Ibn Ezra and Metzudat David read אפקיד as leaving a deposit, so 'God of truth' means He will give it back. Radak reads 'truth' as God keeping His promise that David will be king.

sources.quote: ובעבור שנתנה לפקדון, הזכיר ה' אמת, בעבור הפקדון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says that because the spirit was given as a deposit, the verse mentions the God of truth, because of the deposit.

sources.quote: כי אתה אל אמת להחזיר הפקדון
sources.says: Metzudat David says that You are a God of truth, to return the deposit.

sources.quote: ואמת שתקים דברך שאמרת שאני אמלוך
sources.says: Radak says the truth is that God will keep His word, which He said, that David would reign.

31:6.headline: פדית sounds past: has God already rescued him, or will He?
31:6.body: Rashi reads it as past: David leaves his spirit with God always because God already saved him from trouble. Radak and Metzudat David say it is a past form standing for the future: God will rescue him.

sources.quote: אַפְקִיד רוּחִי תָּמִיד לְפִי שֶׁאַתָּה פָּדִיתָה אוֹתִי מִצָּרָה
sources.says: Rashi says I leave my spirit always, because You redeemed me from trouble.

sources.quote: פדיתה אותי עבר במקום עתיד
sources.says: Radak says פדיתה אותי is the past in place of the future.

sources.quote: פדיתה. עבר במקום עתיד ור״ל הן ידעתי שתפדה אותי ממות
sources.says: Metzudat David says פדיתה is the past in place of the future, meaning: I know that You will redeem me from death.

31:7.headline: השמרים הבלי שוא: who are the people who 'guard' empty things?
31:7.body: Metzudat Zion says שומרים here means those who look and wait, like ואביו שמר את הדבר. Ibn Ezra and Radak say these are people who watch omens and ask soothsayers.

sources.quote: השומרים. המצפים כמו ואביו שמר את הדבר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says השומרים means those who look out, like ואביו שמר את הדבר.

sources.quote: הניחוש והקסם אי זה יום יצא למלחמה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means omens and sorcery about which day to go out to war.

sources.quote: כי בברחי מפני שאול לא שאלתי למנחשים ולהברי שמים על טלטולי
sources.says: Radak says that when he fled from Saul he did not ask the soothsayers and astrologers about his wandering.

31:9.headline: הסגרתני: handed over, or shut in?
31:9.body: Metzudat Zion reads it as handed over, like להסגיר לאדום. Ibn Ezra reads it as shut in, like a man locked up, which is why he says במרחב, a wide place, is its opposite.

sources.quote: הסגרתני. מסרתני כמו להסגיר לאדום
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says הסגרתני means You delivered me, like להסגיר לאדום.

sources.quote: מגזרת סגירה, כאדם נסגר נתון למוסרה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is from the language of closing, like a man shut in and given to a prison.

sources.quote: במרחב רגלי - שילך למקום שיאהב, הפך הסגרתני
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says במרחב רגלי means that he can go to a place he loves, the opposite of הסגרתני.

31:10.headline: עששה: his eye grew dim, or rotted?
31:10.body: Rashi reads עששה as dimming, like an עששית, a glass through which things look unclear. Radak reads it as rotting, from עש, the moth, and for the same root in verse 11 Rashi says rot too.

sources.quote: כָּהֲתָה, לְשׁוֹן עֲשָׁשִׁית. שֶׁאָדָם נוֹתֵן זְכוּכִית לְנֶגֶד עֵינָיו לִרְאוֹת לְעֵבֶר הַזְּכוּכִית דָּבָר, אֵין אוֹתָהּ מַרְאָה בְּרוּרָה
sources.says: Rashi says it dimmed, from the language of עששית, a glass a person puts before his eyes to see something beyond it, which does not show clearly.

sources.quote: עששה מגזרת עש יאכלם
sources.says: Radak says עששה is from the same root as עש יאכלם, the moth that eats them.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן רָקָב, כְּאִלּוּ אֲכָלָם עָשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says of עששו in verse 11 that it is the language of rot, as if a moth ate them.

31:14.headline: דבת רבים: the plotting of many, or their slander?
31:14.body: Rashi says דבת רבים is the counsel of many, from the word for speaking, as in דובב שפתי ישנים. Metzudat Zion says it is saying evil talk about someone, like ויבא את דבתם.

sources.quote: דִּבַּת רַבִּים. עֲצַת רַבִּים
sources.says: Rashi says דבת רבים means the counsel of many.

sources.quote: דִּבַּת לְשׁוֹן ״דּוֹבֵב שִׂפְתֵי יְשֵׁנִים״
sources.says: Rashi says דבת is the language of דובב שפתי ישנים.

sources.quote: אמירת דבת הרע כמו ויבא את דבתם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the saying of evil talk, like ויבא את דבתם.

31:18.headline: ידמו לשאול: struck silent, or cut off?
31:18.body: Rashi reads ידמו as 'be silent': struck dumb on the way to death. Radak reads it as 'be cut off', like אל תדמו בעונה, and Metzudat David agrees.

sources.quote: יִשְׁתַּתְּקוּ וְיֵאָלְמוּ לָמוּת
sources.says: Rashi says they will be silent and struck dumb, to die.

sources.quote: ידמו לשון כריתה
sources.says: Radak says ידמו is the language of cutting off.

sources.quote: ידמו. יכרתו לרדת לשאול
sources.says: Metzudat David says ידמו means they will be cut off, to go down to Sheol.

31:19.headline: עתק: a lie, or a hard and strong word?
31:19.body: Rashi says עתק means a false thing, one that is not so, and compares ויעתק משם. Dunash in Rashi, and Radak, read it as a hard, strong word.

sources.quote: עָתָק. סָרָה, דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says עתק is a falsehood, a thing that is not so.

sources.quote: וְדוּנָשׁ פָּתַר אוֹתוֹ לְשׁוֹן דָּבָר גָּדוֹל וְקָשֶׁה
sources.says: Rashi says Dunash explained it as the language of a great and hard thing.

sources.quote: עתק דבר עתק וחזק
sources.says: Radak says עתק is a word that is עתק and strong.

31:20.headline: נגד בני אדם: in the open, or in spite of people?
31:20.body: Ibn Ezra says it means in the open: God has done many good things for those who trust Him where everyone can see. Meiri offers two readings: against their will, or before everyone's eyes.

sources.quote: וכבר עשית כמה טובות בגלוי לחוסים בך, וזה טעם נגד בני אדם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says You have already done many good things openly for those who trust in You, and that is the meaning of נגד בני אדם.

sources.quote: נגד בני אדם ר״ל על כרחם או פירושו לעין כל
sources.says: Meiri says נגד בני אדם means against their will, or it means before the eyes of all.

31:21.headline: מרכסי איש: bands of plotters, or human pride?
31:21.body: Rashi reads it as bands of wicked men tied together to do harm. Radak and Metzudat Zion read it as heights, like והרכסים לבקעה, so the pride of people.

sources.quote: מֵחֲבוּרֵי רְשָׁעִים הַמִּתְקַשְּׁרִים יַחַד לְהָרַע לָהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it means from the groups of wicked people who bind together to harm them.

sources.quote: מרכסי איש מגאות בני אדם ומגבהותם
sources.says: Radak says מרכסי איש is from the pride of people and their loftiness.

sources.quote: ענין גבהות וכן והרכסים לבקעה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is about height, like והרכסים לבקעה.

31:22.headline: בעיר מצור: the real city Keilah, or a picture of safety?
31:22.body: Rashi says the city is Keilah, where Saul thought David was shut in. Radak says it is a picture: David felt raised up, as if in a fortified city, since מצור can mean strength.

sources.quote: בִּקְעִילָה, כְּשֶׁאָמַר שָׁאוּל עָלַי ״נִסְגַּר לָבוֹא בְּעִיר דְּלָתַיִם וּבְרִיחַ״
sources.says: Rashi says it was in Keilah, when Saul said of me that he is shut in, having come into a city of doors and bars.

sources.quote: הייתי נשגב כאלו הייתי בעיר מצור. ומצור ענין חוזק
sources.says: Radak says I was raised up as if I had been in a fortified city, and that מצור means strength.

31:23.headline: נגרזתי: chopped off by an axe, or driven out?
31:23.body: Dunash in Rashi, Radak and Metzudat Zion tie it to גרזן, an axe: I was chopped off. Menachem, in Rashi, ties it to נגרשתי: I was driven out.

sources.quote: כָּךְ פֵּרֵשׁ דּוּנַשׁ. וּמְנַחֵם חִבְּרוֹ כְּמוֹ ״נִגְרַשְׁתִּי״
sources.says: Rashi says Dunash explained it this way, and Menachem linked it to נגרשתי.

sources.quote: נגרזתי מנגד עיניך כמו: נגזרתי מענין גרזן
sources.says: Radak says נגרזתי is like נגזרתי, from the sense of an axe.

sources.quote: נגרזתי. מל׳ גרזן ור״ל נכרתי כדבר הנכרת בגרזן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says נגרזתי is from גרזן, meaning I was cut off like something cut with an axe.

31:24.headline: על יתר: a bowstring, or the excess of their pride?
31:24.body: Rashi says יתר is a bowstring: God repays measure for measure, like an arrow aimed on the string. Metzudat David reads it as the excess of the proud man's pride, and Ibn Ezra as the rest of the proud.

sources.quote: מִדָּה בְּמִדָּה, מְכֻוֶּנֶת כְּחֵץ עַל יֶתֶר הַקֶּשֶׁת
sources.says: Rashi says measure for measure, aimed like an arrow at the string of the bow.

sources.quote: על יתרון הגאות של עושי הגאוה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is about the excess of the pride of those who act proudly.

sources.quote: על יתר - הנותרים מאנשי הגאוה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says על יתר means those who are left of the proud.

32:3.headline: החרשתי: silent about what?
32:3.body: Rashi says David was silent about confessing his sins, the Targum says about words of Torah, and Metzudat David says he fell silent to think over his deeds.

sources.quote: כַּאֲשֶׁר הֶחֱרַשְׁתִּי מִלְּהִתְוַדּוֹת עַל פְּשָׁעַי לְפָנֶיךָ
sources.says: Rashi says it means when I was silent and did not confess my offenses before You.

sources.quote: מְטוּל דְשַׁתְקֵית מִן פִּתְגָמֵי אוֹרַיְתָא
sources.says: The Targum says it was because I was silent from the words of the Torah.

sources.quote: כאשר החרשתי ועמדתי בשתיקה להתבונן במעשי
sources.says: Metzudat David says that when he stood in silence to look into his deeds, he worried over his sins.

32:6.headline: לעת מצא: when God is found, or when the heart is found?
32:6.body: Rashi reads it as the time when God can be found, ready to accept the prayer. Radak reads it as the time when a person's heart is found free and whole in repentance.

sources.quote: בְּהִמָּצְאֲךָ לְקַבֵּל תְּפִלָּתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means when You are to be found to accept his prayer.

sources.quote: לעת שימצא לבו פנוי, שיהיה לבו שלם בתשובה
sources.says: Radak says it means the time when his heart is found free, when his heart is whole in repentance.

32:6.headline: שטף מים רבים: what are the great waters?
32:6.body: For Rashi the rushing waters are the nations, for Radak they are many troubles, and Ibn Ezra offers death and sickness.

sources.quote: שֶׁלֹּא יִפֹּל בְּיַד הָאֻמּוֹת, שֶׁהֵם כְּמַיִם שׁוֹטְפִים
sources.says: Rashi says it means that he will not fall into the hand of the nations, who are like rushing waters.

sources.quote: צרות רבות, דומות לשטף מים רבים ששוטפים הכל
sources.says: Radak says many troubles are like a flood of many waters that sweep everything away.

sources.quote: או המות והתחלואים והמשילם למים שהתגברו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it may be death and sicknesses, which he compares to waters that grew strong.

32:8.headline: איעצה עליך עיני: I will advise, or I will wink?
32:8.body: Radak reads it as advice, from עצה, drawn from what David saw with his own eyes. Rashi reads it as the winking of an eye: David will signal with his eye what to do.

sources.quote: אתן לך עצה ממה שראיתי בעיני ובעצמי
sources.says: Radak says he will give advice from what he saw with his own eyes.

sources.quote: אֶרְמֹז לְךָ בְּעֵינִי רֶמֶז מַה תַּעֲשֶׂה, אִיעֲצָה לְשׁוֹן קְרִיצַת עַיִן
sources.says: Rashi says he will hint to you with his eye what to do, and that איעצה is the language of winking.

32:10.headline: והבוטח בה': trusting God means what?
32:10.body: Radak says trusting God means knowing there is no support but Him, and so turning back from sin. Ibn Ezra says it means not leaning on doctors, as Asa did.

sources.quote: ויבין שאין לו משען בלעדיו, צריך לו לשוב מחטאיו
sources.says: Radak says that one who trusts in God understands he has no support but Him, and must turn back from his sins.

sources.quote: וטעם והבוטח בה' - שלא ישען על הרופאים כאסא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says והבוטח בה' means that he should not lean on the doctors, as Asa did.

32:11.headline: והרנינו: the righteous are told to make others sing
32:11.body: Radak says the verb reaches out to someone else: the righteous are to make the upright of heart sing with joy. Meiri also says they should gladden them by telling them the news.

sources.quote: והרנינו פעל יוצא
sources.says: Radak says והרנינו is a verb that goes out to another.

sources.quote: שתשמחו אותם בהודיעכם להם כן
sources.says: Meiri says it means that you should make them glad by telling them so.

33:1.headline: Praise is beautiful for the upright, or longed for
33:1.body: Metzudat Zion reads נאוה as beautiful and fitting. Ibn Ezra derives it from תאוה, desire, and also reports the reading from נאה, the later Hebrew word for beautiful.

sources.quote: ונאוה - מגזרת תאוה והנו"ן לבנין נפעל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says נאוה comes from the root of תאוה, desire.

sources.quote: ויש אומרים: כמו נאה בלשון גמרא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports that others read it like נאה, “beautiful,” in the language of the Talmud.

sources.quote: נאוה. מלשון נאה ויפה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says נאוה means fitting and beautiful.

33:3.headline: Why the song must be new
33:3.body: The commentators ask why the song has to be new. Radak says to keep making new songs all the time. Midrash Tehillim says it is for the One who did something new: He left the heavens to dwell on earth in the sanctuary.

sources.quote: שירו לו שיר חדש חדשו לו שיר תמיד
sources.says: Radak says to make God a new song all the time.

sources.quote: שירו לו שיר חדש. למי שעשה חדשה שהניח שמים ושיכן בארץ
sources.says: The midrash says the new song is for the One who did a new thing, leaving the heavens to dwell on earth.

33:6.headline: God’s “word” here means God’s will, not speech
33:6.body: Maimonides says God does not speak with a mouth. “By the word of God the heavens were made” is a figure, like “the breath of His mouth.” It means they came into being by God’s will alone.

sources.quote: כשם ש"פיו" ו"רוח פיו" הם השאָלה, כך "דברו" ו"מאמרו" הם השאלה. והכוונה היא שהם נוצרו מתוך כוונתו וחפצו
sources.says: Maimonides says “His word” is a figure of speech, like “His mouth,” and means the heavens were made by His intent and will.

sources.quote: בדימוי לפעולות היוצאות מן המלכים, שהכלי שלהם לביצוע רצונם הוא הדיבור. והוא יתעלה אינו נזקק לכלי לפעול באמצעותו
sources.says: Maimonides says the verse borrows the picture of a king who acts by giving orders, but God needs no tool to act.

33:7.headline: The sea gathered like a heap, or like a water-skin
33:7.body: Rashi and Radak read כנד as a tall heap, the word used for the sea standing up in Exodus 15. The Aramaic Targum reads it as a water-skin, and Rashi says plainly that נד and נאד, a skin bottle, are not the same word.

sources.quote: כַּנֵּד. לְשׁוֹן גּוֹבַהּ
sources.says: Rashi says כנד means height.

sources.quote: וְאֵין ׳נֵד׳ וְ׳נֹאד׳ שָׁוִין
sources.says: Rashi says נד, a heap, is not the same as נאד, a skin bottle.

sources.quote: ואמרו כנד שהוא התל והערמה כמו (שמות טו ח): נצבו כמו נד נזלים
sources.says: Radak says כנד means a mound or pile, as in the Song of the Sea.

sources.quote: דְמַכְנִיס הֵיךְ זִיקָא מוֹי דְיַמָא
sources.says: The Targum translates: who gathers the waters of the sea like a water-skin.

33:15.headline: The One who forms hearts, or who stores them up
33:15.body: Radak first reads היצר as the One who forms their hearts, so He knows them. He also offers a reading from אוצר, a storehouse: all hearts are kept in God’s treasury. Meiri gives both readings.

sources.quote: היצר יחד לבם כי מי שיצר לבם באמת ידעם
sources.says: Radak says the One who formed their hearts surely knows them.

sources.quote: ויש לפרש היצר כמו (זכריה יא יג): ואשליך אתו בית יי' אל היוצר שהוא כמו: האוצר
sources.says: Radak says היצר can also mean the treasury, as in Zechariah 11:13.

sources.quote: וי״מ בו לשון יוצר ממש
sources.says: Meiri reports both the treasury reading and the plain reading of one who forms.

33:15.headline: All hearts judged in one glance
33:15.body: The sages read יחד, together, as “at one time”: on the day of judgment God sees everyone in a single look. Meiri also gives a plainer reading: God formed every one of them, with none left out.

sources.quote: וְדָרְשׁוּ מִכָּאן שֶׁכֻּלָּן נִסְקָרִין בִּסְקִירָה אַחַת
sources.says: Rashi says the sages learned from here that all people are reviewed in one single look.

sources.quote: ואין המכוון במלת יחד בשעה אחת אבל שהוא יצר את כלם אין מהם א׳ שלא יצרו
sources.says: Meiri reports a view that יחד does not mean “at one time” but that God formed all of them, with none left out.

34:6.headline: ונהרו: their faces shine, or they stream toward God
34:6.body: Rashi and Ibn Ezra read ונהרו as light: the faces of those who look to God light up. Radak reads it from נהר, a river: they run to God the way a river flows.

sources.quote: וְנָהָרוּ. הֵאִירוּ פְנֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says ונהרו means their faces lit up.

sources.quote: ונהרו - יאורו פניהם הפך אל יחפרו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says their faces will shine, the opposite of being ashamed.

sources.quote: ויש אומרים: מגזרת ונהרו אליו - מגזרת נהר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra adds that some take it from נהר, a river, as in 'they will stream to him'.

sources.quote: שענינו ההליכה במרוצה כמו הנהר
sources.says: Radak says it means moving at a run, like a river.

34:10.headline: An odd vowel keeps יראו 'fear' apart from 'see'
34:10.body: The same letters can mean 'they will see'. Ibn Ezra and Radak say the word is pointed in an unusual way, with a silent א, so it cannot be mixed up with 'see'. It means 'fear the LORD'.

sources.quote: ולהפריד בינו ובין יראו, מן ראה, הניחו האל"ף
sources.says: Radak says the א was left silent to keep this word apart from יראו meaning 'see'.

sources.quote: רק בא משונה בעבור שלא תתערב עם יראו צדיקים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word is pointed oddly so it will not be confused with 'the righteous will see'.

sources.quote: יִרְאוּ. יִהְיוּ יְרֵאִים, לְשׁוֹן צִוּוּי
sources.says: Rashi says יראו is a command: be afraid.

34:11.headline: כפירים: young lions, or people who deny God
