sources.says: Radak says the word comes from "I see him," because the enemy looks on for harm.

sources.quote: מִן בִּגְלַל תּוּשְׁבְּחִי
sources.says: The Targum renders the phrase "for the sake of my praise."

5:10.headline: הוות: ruin, or schemes they hope will come true?
5:10.body: Metzudat Zion reads הוות as ruin, and Rashi as plans of harm and deceit. Ibn Ezra ties it to הוה, "to be": evil thoughts they hope will come to be.

sources.quote: הוות. שבר כמו עד יעבור הוות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says הוות means ruin.

sources.quote: וְהוּא לְשׁוֹן מַחֲשֶׁבֶת שֶׁבֶר וְתַרְמִית
sources.says: Rashi says the word means plans of ruin and deceit.

sources.quote: הוות - מגזרה הוה להם למלך כי יחשבו מחשבות רעות, אולי תהיינה ותקומנה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from the verb "to be": they think evil thoughts, hoping they will come to be.

5:11.headline: האשימם: find them guilty, make them miss, or lay them waste?
5:11.body: Radak says some read האשימם as "lay them waste," from שממה, and he also reads it as their plans failing. Meiri offers "hold them guilty" or "make them miss their aim."

sources.quote: יש מפרשים: מלשון שממה; ואשם ושמם כענין אחד
sources.says: Radak says some read it as desolation, since אשם and שמם have the same meaning.

sources.quote: האשימם בעצתם, כלומר שלא יתכן ולא יזדמן להם מה שחשבו לעשות עלי
sources.says: Radak says it can mean that what they planned against David will not work out.

sources.quote: העמידם בחזקת אשמים
sources.says: Meiri says it means let them be known as guilty.

sources.quote: או פירושו החטיאם ממחשבתם
sources.says: Meiri says it may instead mean make them miss what they planned.

5:13.headline: A shield on three sides, and God's favor on the fourth
5:13.body: Rashi says a צנה is a shield that wraps around a person on three sides. The midrash asks what guards the fourth side, and answers with this verse: God's favor surrounds the righteous.

sources.quote: הַמַּקֶּפֶת שָׁלֹשׁ רוּחוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם
sources.says: Rashi says the צנה surrounds a person on three sides.

sources.quote: שהוא מקיף את האדם משלש רוחותיו. ומנין לרבות רוח הרביעי
sources.says: The midrash says the shield covers three sides, and asks how the fourth side is covered, answering with this verse.

51:3.headline: פשעי: 'my sins' in the plural, for Bathsheba and Uriah
51:3.body: David is speaking of one affair, yet he says 'my sins'. Radak, Ibn Ezra and Meiri say it held two sins: taking Bathsheba and causing Uriah's death.

sources.quote: או פירושו כי בזה הפשע היו שנים דבר בת שבע ודבר אוריה
sources.says: Radak says this one sin was really two: the matter of Bathsheba and the matter of Uriah.

sources.quote: וטעם פשעי – בעבור דבר בת שבע ודבר אוריה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'my sins' refers to the matter of Bathsheba and the matter of Uriah.

sources.quote: שמה שאותו עון היה כולל לשתי עונות דבר בת שבע וסבת מות אוריה
sources.says: Meiri says that one sin included two: Bathsheba, and causing Uriah's death.

51:4.headline: הרב: 'increase your mercy and wash me', or 'wash me thoroughly'
51:4.body: The word is written הרבה but read הרב. Radak gives two readings, a command 'do much' or 'wash me very well', and says sin sits in the soul like a stain on cloth.

sources.quote: הרבה. כתוב וקרי הרב ואחד הוא
sources.says: Radak says it is written הרבה and read הרב, and both mean the same.

sources.quote: פי' הרב רחמך וכבסני מעוני או יהיה הרב שם כמו הרבה כלומר מאד כבסני מעוני כי העון בנפש כמו הכתם בבגד
sources.says: Radak says it means 'increase your mercy and wash me', or 'wash me very much', because sin in the soul is like a stain on a garment.

sources.quote: הרב - לשון ציווי, כמו הרף ואגידה לך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says הרב can be a command, like 'stop, and let me tell you'.

51:5.headline: נגדי: David keeps his sin always in front of him
51:5.body: Rashi says regret makes the sin feel always before his eyes. The Midrash says God does not forgive one who puts his sin out of sight, and Maimonides draws a rule from this verse: a sinner should always remember his sin.

sources.quote: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁאֲנִי מִתְחָרֵט וְדוֹאֵג עָלָיו, דּוֹמֶה לִי כְּאִלּוּ הוּא לְפָנַי תָּמִיד
sources.says: Rashi says that because he regrets and worries over it, it seems to be before him all the time.

sources.quote: כך כל המעביר עוונו מנגד עיניו אין הקב"ה מוחל לו לכך אמר דוד וחטאתי נגדי תמיד
sources.says: The Midrash says God does not forgive one who puts his sin out of sight, and so David said 'my sin is always before me'.

sources.quote: שיתקבע בנפשו של כל חוטא שעליו לזכור ולהזכיר תמיד את חטאו, כמו שנאמר
sources.says: Maimonides says these offerings aim to fix in every sinner's mind that he must always remember his sin, as this verse says.

51:6.headline: לבדך: why David says he sinned against God alone
51:6.body: He also wronged Uriah. Radak says only God knew of the sin and Uriah is now dead, while Rashi says even the harm to Uriah was a sin against God, who had forbidden it.

sources.quote: כי דבר בת שבע בסתר היה ואין יודע זולתך
sources.says: Radak says the Bathsheba affair was done in secret and no one knew but God.

sources.quote: אבל עתה שהוא מת לך לבדך חטאתי
sources.says: Radak says that now that Uriah is dead, the sin stands before God alone.

sources.quote: וְאַף מַה שֶּׁהֲרֵעוֹתִי לְאוּרִיָּה (שמואל ב יא) לֹא חָטָאתִי אֶלָּא לְךָ, שֶׁהִזְהַרְתָּ עַל הַדָּבָר
sources.says: Rashi says even the harm he did to Uriah was a sin only against God, who had warned against it.

51:7.headline: בעוון: spelled in full, because no one is free of sin
51:7.body: Here עוון is written with two ו letters. Radak cites Rabbi Acha: the full spelling teaches that even the most pious person has some trace of sin.

sources.quote: בעוון. מלא ויש בו דרש רבי אחא אומר בעון מלא אפילו חסיד שבחסידים א"א שלא יהא לו צד עון
sources.says: Radak says the word is spelled in full, and cites Rabbi Acha: even the most pious cannot be without some trace of sin.

sources.quote: והוא שדרשו בעוון מלא מלמד שאין לך חסיד בכל החסידים שלא היה לו צד אחד בעון
sources.says: Meiri cites the same teaching: the full spelling shows there is no pious man without some trace of sin.

51:7.headline: יחמתני: conceived in heat, a strange word Ibn Ezra stops on
51:7.body: The verb comes from heat, as when the flocks 'came into heat' in Genesis. Ibn Ezra calls the form strange, and cites a view that it hints at Eve, who gave birth only after she sinned.

sources.quote: יֶחֱמַתְנִי. לְשׁוֹן חֲמִימוּת, כְּמוֹ (בראשית ל:לח) ״וַיֵּחַמְנָה הַצֹּאן בְּבֹאָן לִשְׁתּוֹת״
sources.says: Rashi says it is the language of heat, as in 'the flocks came into heat when they came to drink'.

sources.quote: ומלת יחמתני – זרה כאילו יחמה ממני על דרך: ליחמנה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra calls the word יחמתני strange and compares it to ליחמנה, 'to be in heat'.

sources.quote: ויש אומרים: כי זה רמז לחוה שלא ילדה רק אחר שחטאה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites some who say it hints at Eve, who gave birth only after she had sinned.

51:8.headline: בטחות: truth in the 'inner parts', the hidden kidneys
51:8.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion say this rare word means the kidneys, smooth and coated (טוחות) in fat. Ibn Ezra says it means the hidden places of the heart, and Menachem links it to reach, as in a bowshot.

sources.quote: בַּטֻּחוֹת. אֵלּוּ כְּלָיוֹת, שֶׁהֵן חֲלָקוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says בטחות are the kidneys, which are smooth.

sources.quote: בכליות הטוחות ומכוסות בחלב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means the kidneys, which are coated and covered in fat.

sources.quote: בטוחות - המקומות הנעלמים שהם מכוני הלב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means the hidden places that are the seat of the heart.

sources.quote: וּמְנַחֵם חִבְּרוֹ עִם ״כִּמְטַחֲוֵי קֶשֶׁת״
sources.says: Rashi says Menachem links it to 'about a bowshot away'.

51:9.headline: תחטאני: from the word for sin, but meaning 'un-sin me'
51:9.body: חטא means to sin, yet here the verb means to take sin away. Metzudat Zion compares it to שרש, which in Job means to uproot.

sources.quote: תחטאני. תסיר חטאי וכן ובכל תבואתי תשרש (שם לא) ור״ל תסיר השורש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means 'remove my sin', like תשרש in Job, which means to remove the root.

sources.quote: והחיטוי הוא טהרת החטא
sources.says: Radak says this חיטוי is the cleansing of sin.

51:9.headline: באזוב: cleansed with hyssop, as from contact with the dead
51:9.body: Hyssop was used to purify a leper and someone who touched a corpse. The Midrash says one who sins is like one made impure by the dead, and only hyssop cleans him.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּטַהֵר הַמְּצֹרָע וְטָמֵא מֵת
sources.says: Rashi says it is like purifying a leper and one made impure by the dead.

sources.quote: מכאן את למד שכל מי שעובר עבירה כאילו נטמא בנפש מת ואין מטהרין אותו אלא באזוב
sources.says: The Midrash says whoever sins is as if made impure by a corpse, and is purified only with hyssop.

sources.quote: הֵיךְ כֲּהַנָא דְמַדֵי בְאֵזוֹבָא עַל מְסַאֲבָא
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'like the priest who sprinkles with hyssop on one who is impure'.

51:14.headline: ששון ישעך: the lost joy was the holy spirit, or the Torah
51:14.body: Rashi and Radak say the 'joy of your salvation' is the holy spirit, which left David after his sin. The Targum renders it 'return your Torah to me'.

sources.quote: הָשִׁיבָה לִּי שְׂשׂוֹן יִשְׁעֶךָ. רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁנִּסְתַּלְּקָה מֵעָלַי
sources.says: Rashi says it means the holy spirit that had left him.

sources.quote: רוח הקודש היא ששון הנשמה וישעה
sources.says: Radak says the holy spirit is the soul's joy and salvation.

sources.quote: אֲתֵיב לִי אוֹרַיְתָךְ
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'return your Torah to me'.

51:14.headline: נדיבה: a generous spirit, or a noble one?
51:14.body: Metzudat Zion reads נדיבה from נדיב, one who loves to give. Rashi reads it as nobility and rank, and Radak says it is the holy spirit that freely offers songs.

sources.quote: נדיבה. מלשון נדיב האוהב לתת מתן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from נדיב, one who loves to give gifts.

sources.quote: נְדִיבָה. לְשׁוֹן נְדִיבוּת, קְצִינוּת
sources.says: Rashi says it means nobility, high rank.

sources.quote: היא רוח הקודש שמתנדבת דברי שיר לשבח לאל
sources.says: Radak says it is the holy spirit, which freely offers words of song to praise God.

51:16.headline: מדמים: Uriah's blood, or David's own?
51:16.body: Radak reads 'save me from blood' as the guilt for Uriah's blood. Metzudat David reads it as David's own blood, asking not to be killed as punishment.

sources.quote: הצילני. מדמי אוריה שלא תענישני עליהם
sources.says: Radak says it means from Uriah's blood, that God not punish him for it.

sources.quote: מדמים. שלא יושפך דמי בגמול עון הזה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means that my own blood not be shed as payment for this sin.

sources.quote: שֶׁלֹּא אָמוּת בַּחֶרֶב, עַל עָנְשׁוֹ שֶׁל אוּרִיָּה שֶׁהָרַגְתִּי
sources.says: Rashi says it means that I not die by the sword as punishment for Uriah, whom I killed.

51:18.headline: זבח: why David brings no sacrifice for this sin
51:18.body: Rashi and Radak say a sin offering atones only for a sin done by mistake. David sinned on purpose, so only repentance with a broken heart can help.

sources.quote: שֶׁאֵין זֶבַח חַטָּאת בָּא עַל הַמֵּזִיד
sources.says: Rashi says a sin offering is not brought for a deliberate sin.

sources.quote: כי לא צוה האל ית' בקרבנות אלא על השוגג, אבל הוא מזיד היה ואין בו קרבן כי אם תשובה בלב נשבר ונדכא
sources.says: Radak says God commanded offerings only for accidental sins; David's sin was deliberate, so there is no offering for it, only repentance with a broken and crushed heart.

51:21.headline: וכליל: the whole burnt offering, or the priest's grain offering?
51:21.body: כליל means something burned whole. Radak says it may simply repeat 'burnt offering', or mean the priest's grain offering, which was burned entirely; Ibn Ezra and Metzudat Zion take the second view.

sources.quote: עולה וכליל. הוא כפל דבר כי העולה היתה כליל או אמר כליל על מנחת כהן שהיתה כליל
sources.says: Radak says it either repeats the idea, since the burnt offering was burned whole, or refers to the priest's grain offering, which was burned whole.

sources.quote: היא מנחת כהן שנאמר בה כליל תהיה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the priest's grain offering, of which the Torah says 'it shall be burned whole'.

sources.quote: וכליל - מנחת כהן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says וכליל is the priest's grain offering.

52:4.headline: A tongue that thinks
52:4.body: The verse says the tongue plans, though thinking belongs to the heart. Radak says the tongue is the heart’s pen: it shows what the heart thinks.

sources.quote: לפי שהלשון מספרת מחשבת הלב אמר לשונך כאלו הלשון חושבת שהיא קולמוס הלב
sources.says: Radak says the verse speaks as if the tongue thinks because the tongue tells the heart’s thoughts, like the heart’s pen.

sources.quote: בעבור כי הלשון כמו מליץ ועל ידו תראה המחשבה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the tongue is like a spokesman through which the thought is seen.

52:6.headline: Words that swallow, or words said in a whisper
52:6.body: בלע means to swallow. Ibn Ezra says these are words that will swallow and destroy. Metzudat David says they are slander said quietly, as if swallowed. Radak reads them as words of destruction.

sources.quote: אהבת, דברי בלע - שיבלעוך וישחיתוך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says these are words that will swallow you and destroy you.

sources.quote: דברי בלע. הם לשון הרע הנאמר בבליעה ובחשאי
sources.says: Metzudat David says these are slander spoken in a swallowed, quiet way.

sources.quote: אהבת. דברי השחתה כי דבריו השחיתו אחימלך ומשפחתו
sources.says: Radak says these are words of destruction, because Doeg’s words destroyed Ahimelech and his family.

52:7.headline: God will break you, or burn you like coals
52:7.body: Rashi and Meiri read יחתך as breaking. Meiri also reports a reading from the word for raking coals in Proverbs 25: God will burn you.

sources.quote: יַחְתְּךָ. לְשׁוֹן שְׁבִירָה
sources.says: Rashi says יחתך means breaking.

sources.quote: ר״ל ישברך וי״א כמו ישרפך וכמוהו כי גחלים אתה חותה על ראשו
sources.says: Meiri says it means God will break you, and reports others who read it as God will burn you, as with coals in Proverbs.

52:7.headline: The word for “root” here means to uproot
52:7.body: שרש usually means a root. Here it means the opposite: God will pull out every root Doeg has. Ibn Ezra says one form of the verb means to cut out the root, and another means the reverse.

sources.quote: יְשָׁרֵשׁ אַחֲרֶיךָ לַעֲקוֹר כָּל הַשָּׁרָשִׁים
sources.says: Rashi says God will go after you to tear out all the roots.

sources.quote: ויסחך ושרשך מהבנין הכבד. והטעם: להכרית השורש ומבנין הפעול להפך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says in this form ושרשך means to cut off the root, and another form of the verb means the opposite.

52:8.headline: The righteous will see, and they will fear
52:8.body: The verse sets two look-alike words side by side: ויראו, they will see, and וייראו, they will fear. Radak explains: they will see Doeg’s punishment and fear God more.

sources.quote: ויראו צדיקים. הנקמה שיקח האל ממך על דם הכהנים ויוסיפו ליראה מהאל
sources.says: Radak says the righteous will see God’s punishment for the priests’ blood and will fear God more.

sources.quote: וְיֶחְמוּן צַדִיקַיָא בְּפוּרְעָנוּתָא דְרַשִׁיעַיָא וִידַחֲלוּ מִן קֳדָם יְיָ
sources.says: The Targum translates the first word as seeing the punishment of the wicked and the second as fearing God.

54:3.headline: 'Judge me': avenge me, or apply the Torah's runaway law
54:3.body: Rashi and Radak read תדינני as 'take up my cause', that is, avenge me. The Midrash hears a legal plea: the Torah forbids handing a runaway slave back to his master, so God should surely not hand David over to King Saul.

sources.quote: תִּנְקֹם נִקְמָתִי, כְּמוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means avenge me, as in 'the LORD will judge His people' in Deuteronomy 32:36.

sources.quote: אל תסגירני ביד המלך. הוי בגבורתך תדינני. בגבורה של תורה
sources.says: The Midrash has David cite the law against returning a runaway slave and ask God not to hand him over to the king: 'judge me by the strength of the Torah'.

54:7.headline: Written 'the evil will return', read 'He will return it'
54:7.body: The word is written ישוב, 'the evil will come back' by itself, but read aloud as ישיב, 'He will bring it back'. Radak says the meaning ends up the same: the harm they planned falls on them.

sources.quote: ישיב כתיב ישוב, מן הקל והוא פועל עומד טעמו על הרע, וקרי ישיב מן הפעיל וטעמו על האל ית' והענין אחד
sources.says: Radak says the written form makes the evil the subject, the read form makes God the subject, and the meaning is the same.

54:7.headline: A rare word: the ones who keep watching me
54:7.body: לשררי is a rare word. Rashi reads it from 'I see him, but not near' in Numbers 24:17: people who eye David with hostility. Radak says they watched where he stepped and reported it to Saul.

sources.quote: לְעוֹיְנַי, לְשׁוֹן ״אֲשׁוּרֶנּוּ וְלֹא קָרוֹב״
sources.says: Rashi says it means those who eye me with hostility, from the word in Numbers 24:17.

sources.quote: שהם שוררי ומביטים את מקומי אשר תהיה רגלי שם ויגידו לשאול
sources.says: Radak says they watch the place where David's foot is and tell Saul.

55:3.headline: Moaning in pain, or ruling? Two readings of אריד
55:3.body: Rashi reads אריד as moaning in distress, as in "my misery and my wandering (מרודי)" in Lamentations 3:19. He notes that Menachem read it as a word for ruling, as in "rule (ורדו) over the fish of the sea."

sources.quote: אֶתְאוֹנֵן בְּצַעֲרִי, כְּמוֹ ״זְכֹר עָנְיִי וּמְרוּדִי״ (איכה ג:יט), ״וְיָרַדְתִּי עַל הֶהָרִים״ (שופטים יא:לז). וּמְנַחֵם פָּתַר לְשׁוֹן מֶמְשָׁלָה, כְּמוֹ ״וּרְדוּ בִדְגַת הַיָּם״
sources.says: Rashi says אריד means "I moan in my pain," and that Menachem read it as a word for ruling.

sources.quote: וענין אריד היא היללה על החולי או על הצרה
sources.says: Radak says אריד is wailing over illness or trouble.

55:9.headline: A word with no twin in Scripture, read from its setting
55:9.body: Radak says סעה appears nowhere else in Scripture, so it must be read from context. Rashi pictures a storm wind that tears up trees. Metzudat Zion ties it to the verb for moving on (נסע), a wind that drives things away.

sources.quote: ומלת סועה תתפרש לפי מקומה כי סועה אין לה חבר במקרא
sources.says: Radak says the word סועה must be explained from its place, since it has no match in Scripture.

sources.quote: שֶׁהֵם כְּרוּחַ סוֹעָה רוּחַ סְעָרָה עוֹקֶרֶת אִילָנוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says the enemies are like a סועה wind, a storm wind that uproots trees.

sources.quote: סועה. ברוח יאמר לשון הסעה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says סועה, said of wind, comes from moving something along.

55:10.headline: Split their speech, as God did at Babel
55:10.body: David asks God to פלג, divide, the plotters' tongue. Ibn Ezra hears the generation of the Tower of Babel, called דור הפלגה, whose speech God split. Rashi reads it as cutting them off so no one listens to them.

sources.quote: וטעם פלג – שיקרם מה שקרה לדור הפלגה, שכולם התחברו בעיר לעשות לי חמס
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says פלג asks that what happened to the generation of the dispersion happen to them, since they all joined in the city to harm him.

sources.quote: פַּלַּג לְשׁוֹנָם. הַבְדִּילֵהוּ שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁמַע אָדָם לָהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it means cut their speech off so no one will listen to them.

55:12.headline: Blows, or deceit hidden inside the heart?
55:12.body: Rashi reads תך as a blow. Radak reads it as deceit, from תוך, "inside": a man shows with his mouth what is not inside his heart.

sources.quote: תּוֹךְ וּמִרְמָה. לְשׁוֹן מַכָּה
sources.says: Rashi says תוך here means a blow.

sources.quote: תוך. כמו מרמה ונאמר בזה הלשון לפי שמראה בפיו מה שאין בתוך לבו
sources.says: Radak says תוך means deceit, named so because the mouth shows what is not inside the heart.

sources.quote: תוך. מרמה הצפון תוך הלב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says תוך is deceit hidden inside the heart.

55:14.headline: My close friend, or my great one?
55:14.body: Radak reads מידעי as a close friend, someone David told his thoughts and secrets. Rashi reads it like אלופי, "my chief," from "I know you by name," which the Aramaic renders "I made you great."

sources.quote: היותך מיודעי. כלומר רעי שהייתי מודיע אותך דעתי וסודי
sources.says: Radak says מיודעי means my friend, to whom I told my thoughts and secrets.

sources.quote: וּמְיֻדָּעִי. כְּמוֹ אַלּוּפִי, לְשׁוֹן ״וָאֵדָעֲךָ בְשֵׁם״ (שמות לג:יז), דִּמְתַרְגְּמִינָן ״וְרַבִּיתָךְ״
sources.says: Rashi says ומידעי is like אלופי, as in "I know you by name," which the Aramaic renders "I made you great."

55:19.headline: Saved from battle, or from anyone coming near
55:19.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion read קרב as battle, which is also the Aramaic word for war. Meiri also gives the simple reading: from anyone coming near to touch me.

sources.quote: מקרב לי. אני בשלום מכלי קרב ותרגו' כי תצא למלחמה קרבא
sources.says: Radak says it means safe from weapons of war, and the Aramaic renders "war" as קרבא.

sources.quote: מקרב. מלחמה כמו מכלי קרב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says קרב means war.

sources.quote: ויש לפרשו כפשוטו כלומ׳ מהתקרב ומנגוע בי
sources.says: Meiri says it can also be read plainly: from coming near and touching me.

55:22.headline: Drawn swords, or curses?
55:22.body: Metzudat Zion and Ibn Ezra read פתחות as swords, drawn or sharpened. Rashi offers his own reading: a curse, from the Aramaic פתיחא, a writ of ban.

sources.quote: פתחות. חרבות כמו ואת ארץ נמרוד בפתחיה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says פתחות are swords.

sources.quote: חרבות לטושות או שלופות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they are sharpened or drawn swords.

sources.quote: וְאוֹמֵר אֲנִי: לְשׁוֹן קְלָלָה הוּא בִּלְשׁוֹן אֲרַמִּי, כְּדַאֲמַר: כָּתַב אֲמֵימַר פְּתִיחָא עֲלָהּ – וְהוּא שְׁטַר שַׁמְתָּא
sources.says: Rashi says in his view it is an Aramaic word for a curse, like the writ of ban called פתיחא.

55:23.headline: God will carry you, or feed you?
55:23.body: Rashi reads יכלכלך as "He will bear your load," as in "the heavens cannot contain You." The Aramaic Targum reads it as "He will feed you." Ibn Ezra cites the feeding reading from Rabbi Moshe and says it does not fit the psalm.

sources.quote: יְכַלְכְּלֶךָ. יִסְבּוֹל מַשָּׂאֲךָ, כְּמוֹ (מלכים א ח:כז) ״הַשָּׁמַיִם וּשְׁמֵי הַשָּׁמַיִם לֹא יְכַלְכְּלוּךָ״
sources.says: Rashi says יכלכלך means He will carry your burden, as in "the heavens cannot contain You."

sources.quote: וְהוּא יְזוּן יָתָךְ
sources.says: The Targum renders it "and He will feed you."

sources.quote: ורבי משה אמר: נתנך טעמו תנתן לך לחם עד עתה והוא יכלכלך לעתיד, כמו: ויכלכל יוסף. ואין זה מטעם המזמור
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites Rabbi Moshe, who read it as God feeding you as Joseph fed his family, and says this does not fit the psalm.

56:1.headline: David calls himself a dove struck silent, far from home
56:1.body: The title says יונת אלם, a "silent dove". Rashi says David was far from Israel at the Philistine court, like a dove struck dumb. Radak adds that he could only speak like a madman.

sources.quote: וְהוּא הָיָה בֵּינֵיהֶם כְּיוֹנָה אִלֶּמֶת
sources.says: Rashi says David was among the Philistines like a dumb dove.

sources.quote: כיונה הגולה ממקומה והיה אלם ביניהם שלא היה יכול לדבר אלא כדברי משוגע
sources.says: Radak says David was like a dove driven from its place, mute among them, able to speak only like a madman.

sources.quote: דִמְתִילָא לְיוֹנָה שָׁתוֹקָא
sources.says: The Targum says the title compares the community of Israel to a silent dove.

56:1.headline: מכתם can be read as "humble and whole", or as "gold"
56:1.body: Rashi says the sages' reading מך ותם, "humble and whole", fits this psalm's title. Metzudat David hears כתם, "gold": the psalm was as dear to David as fine gold.

sources.quote: שִׁיר זֶה לְדָוִד שֶׁהָיָה מָךְ וְתָם
sources.says: Rashi says that in this psalm the title can be read as a song for David, who was humble and whole.

sources.quote: המזמור הזה היה חביב בעיניו ככתם פז
sources.says: Metzudat David says the psalm was as dear to David as fine gold.

56:3.headline: In verse 3, שאפו may mean "mock" instead of "swallow"
56:3.body: Metzudat David keeps the sense of longing to swallow David. Ibn Ezra says the sense here is like מלעיג, "mocking".

sources.quote: הטעם כמו מלעיג
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the meaning is like מלעיג, mocking.

sources.quote: המסתכלים בי לרעה חושקים לבלעני
sources.says: Metzudat David says those who look at David with ill will long to swallow him.

56:3.headline: In "many fight me, מרום", who is מרום?
56:3.body: Rashi takes מרום as a title for God, who sits on high, so David is calling out to Him. Ibn Ezra reads it as the heights: many angels fight for David from above.

sources.quote: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, שֶׁהוּא יוֹשֵׁב מָרוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says מרום means the Holy One, who sits on high.

sources.quote: ויש לי מלאכים רבים במרום נלחמים בעבורי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says David has many angels on high fighting for him.

sources.quote: אֱלָהָא עִלָאָהּ דִי כּוּרְסֵיהּ בִּמְרוֹמָא
sources.says: The Targum renders it as God on high, whose throne is in the heights.

56:7.headline: יגורו: they gather, or they lodge in ambush?
56:7.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion say the verb means gathering, like יגורו עלי עזים in another psalm. Rashi pictures the enemies lodging in wait where David is expected to walk.

sources.quote: ענין אסיפה וקיבוץ
sources.says: Radak says the word means gathering together.

sources.quote: יאספו כמו יגורו עלי עזים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means they gather, like יגורו עלי עזים.

sources.quote: הֵמָּה אוֹרְבִים וְלָנִים בַּמָּקוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says they lie in ambush and lodge in the place.

57:8.headline: 'My heart is steady' twice: for judgment and for mercy
57:8.body: Radak says the doubling simply adds force. Rashi gives each one a meaning: faithful to God when he judges strictly, and faithful when he shows mercy.

sources.quote: נֶאֱמָן עִמְּךָ בְּמִדַּת הַדִּין וְנֶאֱמָן עִמְּךָ בְּמִדַּת הָרַחֲמִים
sources.says: Rashi says it means faithful to you in strict judgment and faithful in mercy.

sources.quote: מְכַוֵן לִבִּי לְאוֹרַיְתָךְ יְיָ מְכַוֵן לִבִּי לִדְחַלְתָּךְ
sources.says: The Targum renders the two as: my heart is set on your Torah, my heart is set on fearing you.

sources.quote: נכון לבי. הכפל לחזק
sources.says: Radak says the doubling is for emphasis.

57:9.headline: 'Awake, my glory': my honor, or my soul?
57:9.body: Metzudat Zion and Meiri say כבוד here is the soul, the glory of the body. Rashi reads it as David's royal honor: he would not sleep late the way other kings did.

sources.quote: היא הנשמה שהוא כבוד הגוף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the soul, which is the body's glory.

sources.quote: ואומ׳ עורה כבודי כי הנפש יקרא כבוד
sources.says: Meiri says the soul is called כבוד.

sources.quote: וְלֹא אִישַׁן עַד שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁעוֹת בִּכְבוֹדִי כִּשְׁאָר מְלָכִים
sources.says: Rashi says David would not sleep in his honor until the third hour like other kings.

58:3.headline: They weigh out violence as if on honest scales
58:3.body: Metzudat Zion ties תפלסון to פלס, the beam of a balance scale. Ibn Ezra says the judges weigh out their violence so that no one notices it. Radak says they present it as if it were measured fairly.

sources.quote: תפלסון. ענין יושר ועש״ז יקרא מטה המשקל בשם פלס כי מיישר המשקל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says תפלסון means making level, which is why the beam of a scale is called פלס.

sources.quote: וטעם תפלסון – תשקלו אותו עד שלא ירגיש אדם בחמס שתעשו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says תפלסון means they weigh it out so that no one senses the violence they do.

sources.quote: כאלו נעשה בפלס ובמשקל ביושר
sources.says: Radak says they make it seem as if it were done by honest scale and weight.

58:9.headline: A snail that melts as it goes, or a stream of water?
58:9.body: Radak calls the שבלול a snail, a creeping creature that wastes away as it moves. Rashi gives that reading and another: a flowing stream, like שבלת מים. Ibn Ezra cites the sages on a water creature that melts as it moves.

sources.quote: ושבלול הוא שרץ הנקרא בלע"ז לימ"שא
sources.says: Radak says the שבלול is a creeping creature called a snail in the local language.

sources.quote: שַׁבְּלוּל. יֵשׁ פּוֹתְרִין לימצ״א בְּלַעַ״ז, וְיֵשׁ פּוֹתְרִין כְּמוֹ ״שִׁבֹּלֶת מַיִם״
sources.says: Rashi says some explain it as a snail and some as a stream of water.

sources.quote: בדברי הקדמונים ז"ל: ברא שבלול והוא כדמות דג במים שימס בהליכתו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites the early sages: the שבלול is like a fish in water that melts as it moves.

58:9.headline: A woman's stillbirth, or a mole that never sees the sun?
58:9.body: Radak reads אשת as "woman": the wicked will be like a stillborn child that never sees the sun. Rashi brings the sages, who read אשת as a mole, a blind creature called אשותא in Aramaic.

sources.quote: ויהיו כמו נפל האשה כי זה וזה לא ראו שמש
sources.says: Radak says they will be like a woman's stillborn child, which never saw the sun.

sources.quote: שֶׁאֵין לָהּ עֵינַיִם, וְהִיא ״תִּנְשֶׁמֶת״ (ויקרא יא:ל) דִּמְתַרְגְּמִינָן ״אֲשׁוּתָא״, כָּךְ פֵּרְשׁוּהוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ
sources.says: Rashi says the sages read it as a creature with no eyes, the תנשמת, which the Aramaic calls אשותא.

58:10.headline: Alive: in full strength, in health, or raw meat in the pot
58:10.body: Rashi reads חי as strength, and Metzudat Zion as health. Radak continues his cooking picture: the meat in the pot is still raw, "alive," when God's anger sweeps them away.

sources.quote: חַי. לְשׁוֹן גְּבוּרָה
sources.says: Rashi says חי here means strength.

sources.quote: חי. ענין בריאות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says חי means health.

sources.quote: כמו שהבשר אשר בסירותם עודנו חי כי לא הרגישו הסירות מחמימות האטד ולא נתבשל הבשר
sources.says: Radak says it is like meat in the pots that is still raw, because the pots have not yet felt the heat.

59:4.headline: יגורו: the guards camp in his house, or gather against him
59:4.body: Rashi reads יגורו as 'they lodge': Saul's men stayed the night at David's house to guard him. Radak and Ibn Ezra read it as 'they gather' against him.

sources.quote: לָנִים בְּבֵיתִי לְשָׁמְרֵנִי
sources.says: Rashi says they are lodging in my house to guard me.

sources.quote: יאספו ויתקבצו עלי
sources.says: Radak says they gather and assemble against me.

sources.quote: כמו יתקבצו, וכמוהו: העוד הזרע במגורה. ויש אומרים: ישכנו סביב הבית
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means they gather, like מגורה, a storehouse, and notes that others say they live around the house.

59:10.headline: Whose strength? Saul's, say Rashi and Radak; God's, says Ibn Ezra
59:10.body: Rashi and Radak read עזו, 'his strength', as the enemy's: Saul is stronger, so David waits for God. Ibn Ezra reads it as God's own strength.

sources.quote: מפני עוזו של שאול שהוא עז וחזק ממני
sources.says: Radak says it means because of the strength of Saul, who is stronger than David.

sources.quote: עֻזּוֹ וְתָקְפּוֹ שֶׁל אוֹיְבִי הֶחָזָק עָלַי
sources.says: Rashi says it is the strength and power of the enemy who is stronger than David.

sources.quote: עוזו - אתה האל שהעוז לו בעצמו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it refers to God, whose strength belongs to Him by Himself.

59:10.headline: Saul's men guard the house; David keeps watch for God
59:10.body: Verse 1 says Saul's men וישמרו, 'guarded', David's house. Ibn Ezra says David's אשמרה, 'I will keep watch', answers that guarding, and Metzudat Zion says it means waiting.

sources.quote: אליך אשמורה - כטעם ליל שמורים הם כנגד וישמרו את הבית
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says אשמורה is like 'a night of watching' and is set against 'they guarded the house'.

sources.quote: אשמרה. ענין המתנה כמו ואביו שמר את הדבר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says אשמרה means waiting, as in 'his father kept the matter in mind'.

59:11.headline: Written 'His kindness', read 'my kindness': giver and receiver
59:11.body: The word is written חסדו, 'His kindness', but read aloud as חסדי, 'my kindness'. Radak says the meaning is the same: the written form looks at God who gives the kindness, the spoken form at David who receives it.

sources.quote: כתוב חסדו וקרי חסדי ביו"ד והענין אחד אלא שהכתוב על עושה החסד והוא האל יתב' והקרי על המקבלו והוא דוד
sources.says: Radak says it is written חסדו and read חסדי with the same meaning: the written form is about God who does the kindness, the read form about David who receives it.

sources.quote: והכתיב חסדו וביאורו אלהים חסדו יקדמני
sources.says: Meiri says the written form חסדו means 'God, His kindness will come before me'.

59:12.headline: Make them wander, not die, so the lesson is remembered
59:12.body: David asks God not to kill his enemies, because the dead are soon forgotten. Rashi reads הניעמו, 'make them wander', as losing their wealth, a punishment people will remember for a long time.

sources.quote: כִּי כָל הַמֵּתִים מִשְׁתַּכְּחִים, אֶלָּא הֲנִיעֵמוֹ מִנִּכְסֵיהֶם שֶׁיִּהְיוּ עֲנִיִּים, וְהִיא נְקָמָה שֶׁתִּזָּכֵר לְאֹרֶךְ יָמִים
sources.says: Rashi says all the dead are forgotten, so instead God should shake them loose from their property so they become poor, a revenge remembered for a long time.

sources.quote: הניעמו. מל׳ נע ונד
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says הניעמו comes from נע ונד, wandering.

sources.quote: הניעמו - לבקש לחם כאשר הזכיר בכלבים, הם יניעון לאכל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means make them wander to beg for bread, as the psalm says of the dogs, 'they wander to eat'.

59:12.headline: בחילך: by Your strength, or by Your army, Israel
59:12.body: Metzudat Zion reads בחילך as 'by Your strength'. Ibn Ezra and Radak read חיל as an army, and say God's army here is Israel.

sources.quote: בחילך. בכוחך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says בחילך means 'by Your strength'.

sources.quote: וטעם בחילך – הם ישראל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says בחילך means Israel.

sources.quote: ותנידם לבקש לחם בחילך והם ישראל
sources.says: Radak says God should make them wander begging for bread, 'by Your army', which is Israel.

59:12.headline: Calling God 'our shield' hints that God is the real king
59:12.body: Ibn Ezra says מגננו, 'our shield', means our true king. It is a hint aimed at King Saul, who ordered David killed.

sources.quote: מגננו - הוא מלכנו באמת רמז, בעבור שאול המלך שצוה להמיתו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'our shield' is our true king, a hint aimed at King Saul who ordered David's death.

59:13.headline: כחש: lies, or wasting away
59:13.body: The Targum reads כחש as lies. Radak and Metzudat Zion read it as thinness: people will tell each other of the curse and the wasting that comes on the wicked.

sources.quote: אֲרוּם מִן מוֹמָתָא וּמִן שִׁקְרָא יִשְׁתַּעֲיָן
sources.says: The Targum says they speak of oaths and of lies.

sources.quote: ומכחש. רזון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ומכחש means thinness.

sources.quote: ומרוב קללה ומרוב כחש ורזון שיבוא' יספרו בני אדם זה לזה
sources.says: Radak says people will tell each other of the great curse and the great wasting and thinness that will come on them.

59:15.headline: The same words come back, now as the enemies' punishment
59:15.body: Verse 7 says the guards come back each evening to hunt David. Meiri and Metzudat David say verse 15 repeats those words as a curse: now they will roam the city at night begging for bread.

sources.quote: ותחת מה שאמר למעלה ישובו לערב וכו׳ שהיו שם בערב לרגל חזר זה דרך קללה שישובו בערב ויסובבו עיר מרוב העוני לבקש לחם
sources.says: Meiri says that where the psalm earlier said they come back in the evening to spy, it repeats this as a curse: they will come back in the evening and circle the city from poverty, looking for bread.

sources.quote: יענשו מדה במדה כמו ששבו לערב לשמרני וסבבו בעיר לחפש אחרי כן יחזרו על פתחי זולתם לעת ערב
sources.says: Metzudat David says they will be punished measure for measure: as they came back in the evening to guard David and searched the city for him, so they will go from door to door in the evening.

59:17.headline: David sings in the morning, when the night dogs sleep
59:17.body: Saul's men prowl at night like dogs. Ibn Ezra says לבקר, 'in the morning', is the opposite of the dogs, who sleep by day.

sources.quote: ולבקר - הפך הכלבים כי ביום ינומו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'in the morning' is the opposite of the dogs, since they sleep by day.

sources.quote: כְּשֶׁאֶמָּלֵט מֵהֶם לַבֹּקֶר, אָשִׁיר עֻזֶּךָ
sources.says: Rashi says: when I escape from them in the morning, I will sing of Your strength.

59:18.headline: The refrain changes 'I will wait' to 'I will sing'
59:18.body: Verse 10 says עזו אליך אשמרה, 'his strength: I will wait for You'. Radak says verse 18 repeats it after David is saved, with עזי, 'my strength', and אזמרה, 'I will sing'.

sources.quote: ואז אומר עזי במקום עוזו ואליך אזמרה במקום אליך אשמורה כי בעת הצרה אשמור ואקוה התשועה ובעת התשועה אומר ואשיר אליך
sources.says: Radak says David will then say 'my strength' instead of 'his strength' and 'I will sing to You' instead of 'I will wait for You': in trouble he waits, and when saved he sings.

sources.quote: ובעבור זה אמר אחר: אשיר עזך, כי אתה עוזי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says this is why he later says 'I will sing of Your strength', because You are my strength.

6:1.headline: 'On the eighth': an eight-string lyre, or circumcision
6:1.body: Rashi says השמינית is a lyre with eight strings, and Ibn Ezra adds it may be an eighth tune. The sages read it as circumcision, done on the eighth day, which Radak and Meiri call a sermon reading, not the plain sense.

sources.quote: כִּנּוֹר שֶׁל שְׁמוֹנָה נִימִין, וְשְׁמִינִית שְׁמוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it is a lyre of eight strings, and its name is שמינית.

sources.quote: יש אומרים: כלי ניגון, יש לו שמנה יתרים או פיוט יש לו ח' נעימות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some call it an instrument with eight strings, or a song with eight tunes.

sources.quote: והדרש (בבלי מנחות מג ב): על המילה שנתנה בשמינית; וזהו רחוק
sources.says: Radak says the sermon reading is about circumcision, given on the eighth day, and calls it far-fetched.

sources.quote: ואע״פ שרז״ל פירשוהו על המילה שנתנה לשמיני דרך דרש הוא
sources.says: Meiri says the sages read it as circumcision, given on the eighth day, but that is a sermon reading.

6:7.headline: I swim my bed, wash it, or make it foul
6:7.body: Metzudat David reads אשחה as swimming: so many tears that the bed floats on them. Rashi reads it as making the bed foul and loathsome, and Ibn Ezra reports a reading from the Aramaic word for washing.

sources.quote: אני משיט את מטתי במי הבכי כדבר השט על פני המים
sources.says: Metzudat David says I float my bed in the water of my weeping, like something floating on water.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן ״סְחִי וּמָאוֹס״ (איכה ג:מה), ״וְהָיְתָה נִבְלָתָם כַּסּוּחָה״ (ישעיהו ה:כה) – מְמָאֵס אֲנִי מִטָּתִי בִּדְמָעוֹת. וּמְנַחֵם חִבְּרוֹ עִם ״כַּאֲשֶׁר יְפָרֵשׂ הַשֹּׂחֶה לִשְׂחוֹת״
sources.says: Rashi reads it as 'filth and refuse': I make my bed loathsome with tears, and notes that Menachem linked it to swimming.

sources.quote: ויש אומרים: כי אשחה תרגום ארחץ בארמית
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports that some say אשחה is the Aramaic word for 'I wash'.

6:7.headline: My tears soak my couch, or melt it away
6:7.body: Rashi reads אמסה as soaking the couch wet. Radak and Metzudat Zion read it as melting, the word used when a people's heart melts in fear, and Meiri mentions a reading of 'I make it loathsome'.

sources.quote: בְּדִמְעָתִי עַרְשִׂי אַמְסֶה. אֲלַחְלֵחַ וְאַרְטִיב כְּמוֹ מַיִם
sources.says: Rashi says it means I moisten and wet it, like water.

sources.quote: ופרוש אמסה מן המסיו את לב העם
sources.says: Radak says אמסה comes from 'they made the heart of the people melt'.

sources.quote: אמסה. מלשון המסה והתכה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means melting and dissolving.

sources.quote: וי״מ אמסה כמו אמאיס מלשון סחי ומאוס
sources.says: Meiri reports that some read אמסה as 'I make it loathsome', from 'filth and refuse'.

6:8.headline: An eye dimmed as through glass, or eaten by moths
6:8.body: Rashi ties עששה to עששית, glass: the eye sees dimly, as if through glass. Radak and Ibn Ezra tie it to עש, the moth, so the eye has rotted away.

sources.quote: עָשְׁשָׁה. לְשׁוֹן עֲשָׁשִׁית, עַיִן שֶׁמְּאוֹרָהּ כֵּהָה, וְדוֹמֶה לוֹ כְּאִלּוּ הוּא רוֹאֶה דֶּרֶךְ זְכוּכִית
sources.says: Rashi says it is from עששית: an eye whose light is dim, as if seeing through glass.

sources.quote: עששה מגזרת עש יאכלם (ישעיהו נ ט) כאלו אמר רקבה
sources.says: Radak says it comes from 'the moth will eat them', as if to say it has rotted.

sources.quote: עששה - מגזרת עש יאכלם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from 'the moth will eat them'.

6:10.headline: God 'takes' my prayer, as He would take an offering
6:10.body: יקח, 'He will take', here means He will accept, as Radak and Meiri say. Ibn Ezra adds a second reading: God takes the prayer in place of a burnt offering.

sources.quote: וטעם יקח – יקבל או יקחנה תחת עולה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says יקח means He will accept it, or He will take it in place of a burnt offering.

sources.quote: וטעם יקח בזאת העת ובכל עת בבוא תפלתי אליו יקבלנה ברצון
sources.says: Radak says that now and always, when my prayer comes to Him, He will accept it gladly.

sources.quote: ויקח כמו יקבל
sources.says: Meiri says יקח means 'He will accept'.

6:11.headline: They turn back: to be judged again, or to make peace
6:11.body: Rashi asks why the verse says 'they will be ashamed' twice, and brings Rabbi Yochanan: God takes the wicked back for a second judgment, so they are shamed twice. Radak and Ibn Ezra read ישבו as the enemies coming back to make peace, ashamed.

sources.quote: וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַחֲזִירָן וְחוֹזֵר וּמַרְאֶה גִּלְיוֹנִין שֶׁלָּהֶם וְדָן אוֹתָם וּמִתְחַיְּבִין, וְהוּא מַחֲזִירָן לַגֵּיהִנֹּם. הֲרֵי בּוּשָׁה כְּפוּלָה
sources.says: Rashi says God brings them back, shows them their records, judges them again, and returns them to punishment, so the shame is doubled.

sources.quote: ישבו אלי להיות בשלום עמי ובאותו רגע תהיה להם בושת ממני
sources.says: Radak says they will come back to make peace with him, and in that moment they will be ashamed before him.

sources.quote: ישובו - ינחמו או יבקשו שלומי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means they will regret, or they will seek my peace.

60:1.headline: מכתם: fine gold, or David 'humble and whole'
60:1.body: Rashi links מכתם to כתם, fine gold, something precious. He also brings the sages, who split it into מך and תם: David stayed humble and whole even as king.

sources.quote: מִכְתָּם לְשׁוֹן ״כֶּתֶם פָּז״ (שיר השירים ה:יא) דָּבָר חָמוּד
sources.says: Rashi says מכתם comes from כתם, fine gold, meaning something precious.

sources.quote: וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דָּרְשׁוּ עַל דָּוִד שֶׁהָיָה מַנְהִיג עַצְמוֹ כְּמָךְ וְתָם אֲפִלּוּ בְּמַלְכוּתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the sages read it as David behaving humble and whole even in his kingship.

sources.quote: המזמור הזה היה אהוב לו כעדי מכתם פז
sources.says: Metzudat David says the psalm was as dear to David as a gold ornament.

60:2.headline: בהצותו: when he fought, when he ruined, or when he burned?
60:2.body: Rashi reads it as fighting, as in Numbers 26:9. Ibn Ezra reports a reading of 'ruined', and the midrash offers 'set on fire' or 'shot arrows'.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ ״בְּהַצּוֹתָם עַל ה׳״ (במדבר כו:ט), שֶׁנִּלְחַם בָּהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it means he fought them, like 'when they strove against God'.

sources.quote: יש אומרים: בהחריבו מגזרת ערים נצים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports that some read it as 'when he laid waste', from 'ruined cities'.

sources.quote: מהו בהצותו שהציתה באש. דבר אחר שירה בם חצים
sources.says: The midrash says it means he set it on fire, or that he shot arrows at them.

60:4.headline: פצמתה: a one-time word for splitting the land open
60:4.body: This verb appears nowhere else. Radak reads it as splitting open, as in an earthquake, and Rashi reports that Dunash called it an Arabic word.

sources.quote: פצמתה - אין רע לו וטעמו כענין מקומו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word has no partner elsewhere, so its sense comes from the context.

sources.quote: וְרָאִיתִי בְּדִבְרֵי דוּנָשׁ שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן עֲרָבִי, אֲבָל לֹא פֵּרֵשׁ אוֹתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says Dunash called it an Arabic word but did not explain it.

sources.quote: הוא ענין פתיחה ובקיעה ובעת הרעש תפתח הארץ ותבקע
sources.says: Radak says it means opening and splitting, as the ground splits in an earthquake.

60:4.headline: Written like 'let go', meant as 'heal'
60:4.body: רפה with ה usually means to slacken. Rashi and Radak say it stands for רפא, heal: 'heal her broken places'.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן רְפוּאָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּהֵ״א
sources.says: Rashi says it means healing, even though it is written with ה.

sources.quote: ונכתב רפה בה"א במקום אל"ף
sources.says: Radak says רפה is written with ה in place of א.

60:5.headline: יין תרעלה: wine that wraps up and blocks the heart
60:5.body: Rashi takes תרעלה from רעל, wrapping, like a veil: a wine that closes the heart. Metzudat Zion ties it to ערל, blocked, and the midrash hears wine that stirs people to throw off the yoke of Torah.

sources.quote: הָאוֹטֵם אֶת הַלֵּב וְעוֹטְפוֹ. רַעַל לְשׁוֹן עֲטִיפָה הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says it is wine that blocks and wraps the heart, since רעל means wrapping.

sources.quote: מל׳ ערל ואטום כמו ערלה אזנם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from 'closed and blocked', as in 'their ear is closed' (Jeremiah 6:10).

sources.quote: יין שהוא מתער את העולם שיתיר עולה של תורה
sources.says: The midrash reads it as wine that stirs the world to loosen the yoke of Torah.

60:6.headline: נס להתנוסס: a banner to raise, or a trial to test?
60:6.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion read נס as a raised flag: God lifts his people high. Rashi reads it as a test: God gives the faithful hard trials to see if they stay true.

sources.quote: לִהְיוֹת מְנֻסִּים בָּהֶם, אִם יַעַמְדוּ בְּיִרְאָתֶךָ
sources.says: Rashi says it means to be tested by them, to see whether they stay in awe of God.

sources.quote: ענין הרמה והגבהה כנס הגבוה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means raising up, like a high banner.

sources.quote: להתגדל על אויבינו להרים נסנו עליהם
sources.says: Radak says it means to rise over our enemies and lift our banner over them.

60:6.headline: קשט: truth, or making God's ways look fair?
60:6.body: Metzudat Zion and Radak read קשט as truth: God keeps his promise. Rashi reads it as adorning: Israel's trials make God's later kindness look right to the nations.

sources.quote: ענין אמת ותמים כמו קושט אמרי אמת
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means truth, as in Proverbs 22:21.

sources.quote: לְקַשֵּׁט מִדּוֹתֶיךָ בָּעוֹלָם
sources.says: Rashi reads it as 'to adorn your ways in the world', so the nations will not question God's goodness to Israel.

60:8.headline: עמק סכות: a valley's name, or a valley of idols?
60:8.body: Metzudat Zion takes סכות as a place name, and Rashi admits he does not know which place. He also offers 'images', from the idol named in 2 Kings 17:30.

sources.quote: סֻכּוֹת זֶה אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מֵאֵיזֶה אֻמָּה הִיא
sources.says: Rashi says he does not know which nation this Sukkot belongs to.

sources.quote: סֻכּוֹת לְשׁוֹן צוּרוֹת וְדִמְיוֹנוֹת
sources.says: Rashi also offers that סכות means images and figures.

sources.quote: סכות הם שמות מקומות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says Shechem and Sukkot are names of places.

60:10.headline: נעלי over Edom: my shoe, or my lock?
60:10.body: Radak and the Targum read it as a shoe: Edom will be trampled underfoot. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as a bolt, from מנעול: Edom will be locked under David's rule.

sources.quote: נַעֲלִי. מַסְגֵּר שֶׁלִּי
sources.says: Rashi says נעלי means 'my lock'.

sources.quote: מל׳ מנעול העשוי לסגור בו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from מנעול, a lock used to shut.

sources.quote: אשליך נעלי. שיהא מרמס רגלי
sources.says: Radak says it means Edom will be trampled under my feet.

sources.quote: טִלְקֵית מְסָנַי
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'I threw my shoes'.

62:1.headline: Jeduthun heard as “decrees” against Israel
62:1.body: Rashi says ידותון is a musical instrument. The midrash he cites hears the word דתות, decrees, inside it: the psalm is about the harsh laws and judgments enemies impose on Israel.

sources.quote: עַל יְדוּתוּן. שֵׁם כְּלִי שִׁיר, וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה : עַל הַדָּתוֹת וְעַל הַדִּינִין הַנִּגְזָרִים עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאוֹיְבֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says ידותון is the name of an instrument, and the midrash reads it as the decrees and judgments enemies impose on Israel.

62:3.headline: “I will not greatly fall,” or not fall into the deep
62:3.body: Rashi reads רבה as “greatly”: no great fall. He adds a midrash that רבה means Gehinnom, and Ibn Ezra reads it as the great deep. Radak notes that verse 7 repeats the line without רבה, saying “I will not fall” at all.

sources.quote: לֹא אֶמּוֹט רַבָּה. מְטוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת, וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה: רַבָּה גֵּיהִנֹּם
sources.says: Rashi says it means no great falls, and gives a midrash that רבה is Gehinnom.

sources.quote: וטעם לא אמוט – אל תהום
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says “I will not fall” means into the deep.

sources.quote: שיהיה עוד משגבי שלא אמוט כלל, וזה בצאתי מהגלות לפיכך לא זכר רבה
sources.says: Radak says verse 7 leaves out רבה because once out of exile he will not fall at all.

62:4.headline: A one-time word that puzzled the early grammarians
62:4.body: תהותתו appears only here. Rashi gives three readings: Menachem says “gather against,” Rashi links it to הוות, ruin, and others say “talk at length,” comparing Arabic. Meiri also links it to ruin or to gathering.

sources.quote: עַד אָנָה תֵּאָסְפוּ עַל אִישׁ. וְלִי נִרְאֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְפוֹתְרוֹ לְשׁוֹן ״הַוּוֹת״
sources.says: Rashi reports Menachem’s reading “how long will you gather against a man,” and prefers to link the word to הוות, ruin.

sources.quote: וְדִמּוּהָּ לִלְשׁוֹן הָעֲרָב כְּשֶׁמַּרְבֶּה בִּדְבָרִים
sources.says: Rashi reports others who compared it to an Arabic word for talking too much.

sources.quote: ומלת תהותתו נגזרת מן הוות תחשוב לשונו
sources.says: Meiri says תהותתו comes from הוות, ruin, as in Psalm 52.

62:4.headline: One vowel decides: you murder, or you will be murdered
62:4.body: Two old traditions of reading differ by one vowel. Ben Naftali reads “you all murder.” Ben Asher reads “may you all be murdered,” a curse. Radak and Meiri explain both, and Radak follows Ben Asher.

sources.quote: ובן נפתלי תרצחו בפת"ח הרי"ש ואנו סומכין על קריאת בן אשר
sources.says: Radak says Ben Naftali reads the word with a different vowel, and we rely on Ben Asher’s reading.

sources.quote: יהי רצון שתרצחו כולכם ותהיו כקיר נטוי
sources.says: Radak explains Ben Asher’s reading as a curse: may you all be murdered.

sources.quote: ומלת תרצחו לקריאת בן נפתלי בפתחות הריש כלומ׳ שכלכם מרצחים אותנו תמיד
sources.says: Meiri says that by Ben Naftali’s reading it means you all keep murdering us.

62:12.headline: God spoke once, and two things were heard
62:12.body: Radak reads “once, twice” as “many times.” Rashi and the sages read it literally: from one word of God, two things were heard. Maimonides cites this verse for the view that at Sinai Israel heard only one voice.

sources.quote: אחת דבר אלהים. פעם ושתים כלומר פעמים רבות
sources.says: Radak says “once and twice” means many times.

sources.quote: וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דְּרָשׁוּהוּ (מכילתא יתרו בחדש ז) בְּזָכוֹר וְשָׁמוֹר בְּדִבּוּר אֶחָד נֶאֶמְרוּ
sources.says: Rashi says the sages read it as “remember” and “keep” the Sabbath, said in one single word.

sources.quote: כל ישראל לא שמעו במעמד הזה אלא קול אחד בלבד פעם אחת
sources.says: Maimonides says that at Sinai all Israel heard only one voice, one time, and the sages tied this to our verse.

62:13.headline: “Like his deeds” means less than his deeds
62:13.body: Rashi asks where the kindness is in paying people back. He answers from the small letter כ, “like”: God pays back only part of what a person did, not the full amount.

sources.quote: כִּי אַתָּה תְשַׁלֵּם לְאִישׁ כְּמַעֲשֵׂהוּ, וְלֹא מַעֲשֵׂהוּ מַמָּשׁ אֶלָּא מִקְצָתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says God pays a person “like” his deeds, not his actual deeds but only part of them.

63:2.headline: Seeking God, or rising at dawn to pray to Him?
63:2.body: Rashi reads אשחרך as "I will seek you." Ibn Ezra also links it to שחר, dawn, and the Targum and Meiri read it as rising early in the morning to pray.

sources.quote: אֲבַקֵּשׁ וְאֶדְרוֹשׁ לְךָ
sources.says: Rashi says the word means "I will seek you and ask after you."

sources.quote: כמו שוחר טוב, או מגזרת שחר כמו ולבקר בהיכלו מגזרת בקר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means seeking, or else it comes from שחר, dawn, the way "to visit in His temple" comes from בקר, morning.

sources.quote: אֲקוּם בְּצַפְרָא קֳדָמָךְ
sources.says: The Targum translates it "I will rise in the morning before you."

sources.quote: שאקום בשחרים להתפלל לפניך
sources.says: Meiri says it means David will rise at dawn to pray.

63:3.headline: "Your strength" here means the Ark of the Covenant
63:3.body: Ibn Ezra and Metzudat Zion say עזך, "your strength," points to the Ark. Metzudat Zion says the Ark earned this name when it showed God's power among the Philistines.

sources.quote: ואני רואה עוזך שהוא הארון, כמו: ויתן לשבי עזו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says "your strength" is the Ark, as in the verse where God gave "His strength" into captivity.

sources.quote: על הארון יאמר וכמ״ש וארון עוזך (לקמן קלב) על שהראה בפלשתים עוז כח המקום
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word refers to the Ark, because it showed God's strength among the Philistines.

63:6.headline: Lips of song, or many languages of song?
63:6.body: שפה means a lip, but also a language, as in "one language" at the Tower of Babel. Rashi reads "lips of song" as tongues of song, and Ibn Ezra says David will sing in every language he knows.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁל רְנָנוֹת, כְּמוֹ ״וַיְהִי כָל הָאָרֶץ שָׂפָה אֶחָת״
sources.says: Rashi says the word means languages of song, as in "the whole earth was one language."

sources.quote: שארנן לך בכל שפה שאדענה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means "I will sing to you in every language I know."

63:11.headline: Dragged down by the sword, or his blood poured out?
63:11.body: Rashi says יגירהו is a word for dragging. Radak and Metzudat Zion read it as pouring out, because killing by the sword spills blood.

sources.quote: יַגִּירֻהוּ לְשׁוֹן גְּרִירָה
sources.says: Rashi says the word means dragging.

sources.quote: ובא זה הלשון בענין ההריגה מפני הדם הניגר על ידי חרב
sources.says: Radak says the word is used for killing because of the blood that flows from the sword.

sources.quote: ענין הזלה ושפיכה כמו וכמים הנגרים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means flowing and pouring, like spilled water.

64:7.headline: Searching for pretexts, or for wrongs to commit?
64:7.body: Rashi reads עולת as עלילות, 'pretexts,' like the officials in Daniel who looked for a charge against him. Ibn Ezra reads it from עול, 'wrongdoing.'

sources.quote: מְבַקְּשִׁים עֲלִילוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״הֲווֹ בָּעַיִן עִלָּה הַשְׁכָּחָה לְדָנִיֵּאל״
sources.says: Rashi says they search for pretexts, as the officials in Daniel 6:5 sought a charge against Daniel.

sources.quote: עולות - מגזרת עול כמו: ועולתה קפצה פיה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word comes from עול, wrongdoing.

64:7.headline: They finished the plot, or they hid it?
64:7.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion read תמנו as 'they finished,' with the נ standing in for a doubled מ, as in 'His kindnesses are not finished.' Rashi explains it as keeping the plan inside their hearts without showing it.

sources.quote: כמו תממו וכן חסדי ה׳ כי לא תמנו (איכה ג׳:כ״ב) והוא מל׳ תם והשלמה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is like תממו and means finishing, as in Lamentations 3:22.

sources.quote: תמנו כמו תממו הנו"ן במקום אות הכפל
sources.says: Radak says the נ takes the place of a doubled letter, so the word means 'they finished.'

sources.quote: תַּמְנוּ. בְּלִבָּם וְלֹא גִלּוּ דַּעְתָּם
sources.says: Rashi says they kept it in their hearts and did not reveal their intent.

64:8.headline: They shot in secret, so God shoots back
64:8.body: Ibn Ezra and Meiri say וירם answers the plotters' shooting in verse 5: as they shot their arrows, God shoots his. Rashi reads the same verb as 'threw,' since Daniel's accusers were thrown into the lions' den.

sources.quote: ויורם - כנגד לירות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'God shot them' is set against 'to shoot' in verse 5.

sources.quote: כשם שהורוני בחציהם כן יורם א׳ חץ פתאום
sources.says: Meiri says that just as they shot at David with arrows, God will shoot a sudden arrow at them.

sources.quote: יָרָה אוֹתָם לְגוֹב הָאֲרָיוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says God threw them into the lions' den.

64:9.headline: The tongue they sharpened is the tongue that trips them
64:9.body: Ibn Ezra notes this answers verse 4, where they sharpened their tongues like swords. Rashi says the trap they set with their words was turned back on them.

sources.quote: ויכשילוהו - כנגד שננו לשונם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'their tongue tripped them' is set against 'they sharpened their tongue' in verse 4.

sources.quote: הַכִּשָּׁלוֹן שֶׁדִּמּוּ לְהַכְשִׁילוֹ, עָלֵימוֹ נֶהְפַּךְ לְשׁוֹנָם
sources.says: Rashi says the stumbling they planned for him was turned back on them by their own tongue.

64:9.headline: Onlookers shake their heads in scorn, or tremble in fear?
64:9.body: Rashi says everyone who sees them shakes their head and laughs at them. Radak says the onlookers tremble at the sight, and Metzudat Zion ties the word to wandering.

sources.quote: בְּרֹאשָׁם, לְהָנִיעַ רֹאשׁ וְלִשְׂחוֹק עֲלֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says onlookers shake their heads and laugh at them.

sources.quote: מרוב מהומתם ומעלתם יתנודדו ויחרדו כל הרואים המהומות
sources.says: Radak says all who see their panic will shake and tremble.

sources.quote: יתנודדו. מל׳ נדידה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from wandering.

65:2.headline: To You, silence is praise
65:2.body: דומיה means silence. Rashi and Maimonides read the verse as 'silence is Your praise', because any praise we add falls short. Radak reads דומיה as hope: praise waits for You in Zion.

sources.quote: הַשְּׁתִיקָה תְּהִלָּה לְךָ, לְפִי שֶׁאֵין קֵץ לְשִׁבְחֲךָ; וְהַמַּרְבֶּה בְּשֶׁבַח אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא גּוֹרֵעַ
sources.says: Rashi says silence is Your praise, because Your praise has no end, and one who adds praise only takes away.

sources.quote: פירושו: השתיקה לגביך היא השיבוח. וזה לשון הולם מאוד מאוד לגבי העניין הזה
sources.says: Maimonides says the verse means silence is the praise of God, and calls it the most fitting thing said on the subject.

sources.quote: דומיה. ענין תוחלת, אמר לך מיחלת התהלה שתאמר לך בציון בקיבוץ גליות
sources.says: Radak says דומיה means hope: the praise that will be said in Zion when the exiles return is waiting for You.

65:6.headline: You answer us, or you provide for us?
65:6.body: תעננו usually means 'you answer us'. Metzudat David reads it so: God answers with wonders. Meiri reads it as 'you provide for us', like 'the earth shall answer with grain'.

sources.quote: בצדקתך תעננו בדבר הנוראות והנפלאות אשר תעשה עמנו
sources.says: Metzudat David says God in His justice answers us with the awesome wonders He does for us.

sources.quote: ותעננו אצלי לשון הספקה כמו והארץ תענה את הדגן
sources.says: Meiri says that in his view תעננו means providing, as in 'the earth shall answer with grain'.

65:9.headline: Morning and evening each get their own song
65:9.body: The verse says the comings of morning and evening make people sing. Rashi says this is the morning blessing for the One who forms the lights and the evening blessing for the One who brings on evening.

sources.quote: בַּבֹּקֶר אוֹמְרִים בָּרוּךְ יוֹצֵר הַמְּאוֹרוֹת, וּבָעֶרֶב בָּרוּךְ הַמַּעֲרִיב עֲרָבִים
sources.says: Rashi says in the morning people bless the One who forms the lights, and in the evening the One who brings on evening.

sources.quote: המאורות היוצאים להאיר בבוקר ובערב, היציאה ההיא תעורר לב הבריות לרנן לך
sources.says: Metzudat David says the lights rising morning and evening stir people's hearts to sing to God.

65:14.headline: Rams, or open meadows, dressed in flocks
65:14.body: כרים can mean rams or wide pastures. Metzudat Zion reads it as sheep. Radak and Ibn Ezra read it as open plains, covered with flocks like a coat of wool. Ibn Ezra notes the early Sages read the phrase as a polite euphemism, and the Targum says the rams mount the flock.

sources.quote: כרים. כבשים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says כרים means sheep.

sources.quote: לבשו כרים. פירושו מישור
sources.says: Radak says כרים means plains.

sources.quote: וקדמונינו ז"ל פירשוהו: לשון נקייה. והנכון בעיני: כי כרים כמו כר נרחב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the early Sages read it as a polite phrase, but he thinks כרים means wide pasture.

sources.quote: יַעֲלוּן דִכְרַיָא עִלַוֵי עָנָא
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'the rams will mount the sheep'.

66:3.headline: יכחשו: enemies fawn falsely, or confess their own lies
66:3.body: Metzudat David says God's enemies, afraid of His power, will falsely claim to be His friends. Rashi and Ibn Ezra say they will admit the lies and sins they carry.

sources.quote: בעבור רוב חזקך יכחשו לך אויביך לאמר שהמה אוהביך
sources.says: Metzudat David says that because of God's great strength His enemies will lie to Him, saying they are His friends.

sources.quote: הָרְשָׁעִים, מֵרוֹב פַּחַד מוֹדִים עַל כַּחַשׁ וַעֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁבְּיָדָם
sources.says: Rashi says the wicked, out of great fear, admit the lies and sins in their hands.

sources.quote: וטעם יכחשו – שיעידו כי שקר וכחש הוא בידם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says יכחשו means they will testify that falsehood and lies are in their hands.

66:5.headline: עלילה: God's awesome deeds, or God finding fault with people
66:5.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion say עלילה means deeds: God's acts are awesome. Rashi reads the phrase as people fearing God in case He finds a sin in them, since all they do is open to Him.

sources.quote: נורא עלילה. נורא מעשה
sources.says: Radak says נורא עלילה means awesome in deed.

sources.quote: עלילה. מל׳ מעללים ופעולות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says עלילה comes from the word for deeds and actions.

sources.quote: יָראוּי עַל בְּנֵי אָדָם פֶּן יִמְצָא לָהֶם פֶּשַׁע, כִּי כָל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם גְּלוּיִים לְךָ
sources.says: Rashi says God is to be feared by people, in case He finds a sin in them, for all their deeds are open to Him.

66:7.headline: עולם: God rules forever, or God rules the world
66:7.body: Ibn Ezra says עולם in the Bible never means 'world', only time and forever: God rules forever. The Targum and Metzudat David read it as the whole world.

sources.quote: אין עולם בכל זמן בכל המקרא רק זמן ונצח. והטעם: שהשם מושל לעולם כמו מושל נצח
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says עולם anywhere in Scripture means only time and forever, so the sense is that God rules forever.

sources.quote: דְשַׁלִיט בְּכֹחַ גְבוּרְתֵּיהּ עַל עַלְמָא
sources.says: The Targum says God rules with His mighty strength over the world.

sources.quote: עתה הנה מושל בגבורתו על כל העולם
sources.says: Metzudat David says God now rules with His strength over the whole world.

66:9.headline: Kept alive in exile, or given life in the world to come
66:9.body: Radak says בחיים means God kept us alive through the exile. The Targum reads it as the life of the world to come, and Meiri sees a hint at the saving of the soul.

sources.quote: השם נפשינו בחיים. שהשארנו בחיים בגלות
sources.says: Radak says it means God left us alive in exile.

sources.quote: דְמַנֵי נַפְשָׁנָא בְּחַיֵי דְעָלְמָא דְאָתֵי
sources.says: The Targum says God set our soul in the life of the world to come.

sources.quote: שם נפשנו בחיים רמז לתשועת הנפש
sources.says: Meiri says 'set our soul in life' hints at the saving of the soul.

66:10.headline: 'You tested us' is a figure of speech: God already knows
66:10.body: Ibn Ezra says that God testing people to learn what is in their heart is only a way of speaking. Everything is open to God before the thinking heart is even made.

sources.quote: והשם נסה לדעת אשר בלבבם, גם זה דרך משל, כי הכל לפניו גלוי טרם בראותו לב המחשב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says God testing to know what is in their heart is also a figure of speech, since everything is open to Him before He creates the heart that thinks.

66:11.headline: מועקה: a belt pulled tight around the waist
66:11.body: The word appears only here. Meiri says it is a belt pressed tight on the waist, named from עקה, pressure, as in Amos's מעיק, 'I will press you down'.

sources.quote: ומועקה משל על אזור הדבוק במתנים והמהדק אותם וקראה מועקה על שם [עקה] למתנים מרוב ההדוק
sources.says: Meiri says מועקה is a figure for a belt stuck to the waist and squeezing it, called מועקה from the pressure on the waist.

sources.quote: מוּעָקָה. לְשׁוֹן מַסְגֵּר וְכָל הַמֵּעִיק וּהַמֵּצִיק כָּמוֹהוּ
sources.says: Rashi says מועקה means a lock-up, and anything that presses and squeezes.

sources.quote: מועקה. צרה וצוקה כמו מעיק תחתיכם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says מועקה means trouble and distress, as in 'I press you down' (Amos 2:13).

66:17.headline: רומם: I exalted Him, or His praise waits under my tongue
66:17.body: Radak reads ורומם as a verb: I called with my mouth and exalted Him with my tongue. Rashi cites a reading where it is a noun: His praise lies ready under my tongue, waiting to be spoken.

sources.quote: בפי קראתי אליו והוא רומם תחת לשוני כלומר שרוממתי אותו בלשוני
sources.says: Radak says I called Him with my mouth and exalted Him with my tongue.

sources.quote: רוֹמְמוּת שֶׁלּוֹ מוּכָן תַּחַת לְשׁוֹנִי, לְהוֹצִיאוֹ בַּפֶּה
sources.says: Rashi cites a reading in which His exaltation is ready under my tongue, to bring it out with the mouth.

sources.quote: ויותר מרומם היה תחת לשוני רמז ללב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says something even more exalted was under my tongue, a hint at the heart.

66:18.headline: A sinful thought: overlooked by God, or a block to prayer?
66:18.body: Radak and Metzudat David read: even if I thought of doing wrong, God did not count it, since He does not treat a bad thought like a deed. Ibn Ezra reads: had there been wrong in my heart, God would not have heard my prayer.

sources.quote: לא חשבו לי עון שהמחשבה רעה אין הקב"ה מצרפה למעשה
sources.says: Radak says it was not counted against me as sin, because God does not join a bad thought to a deed.

sources.quote: עשה עצמו כאלו לא ישמע ולא יודע מחשבתי כי אינו מצרף מחשבה רעה למעשה
sources.says: Metzudat David says God acted as if He did not hear or know my thought, because He does not join a bad thought to a deed.

sources.quote: אילו היה און בלבי לא היה השם שומע מה שאני קורא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says if there had been wrong in my heart, God would not have heard what I called out.

68:5.headline: God 'rides' the heavens: Maimonides says it means He rules them
68:5.body: Maimonides says רכב first means riding an animal, then was borrowed for ruling, since a rider controls what he rides. So 'the rider on the ערבות' means the one who rules the highest heaven.

sources.quote: א) משמעות שימושו הראשון היא רכיבת האדם על הבהמות כנהוג
sources.says: Maimonides says the first meaning is a person riding an animal.

sources.quote: ב) לאחר מכן הושאל למשילה על דבר, כי הרוכב מושל ושליט על הנרכב
sources.says: Maimonides says it was then borrowed to mean ruling over something, because the rider rules what he rides.

sources.quote: משמעותו: המושל על ערבות, שהוא הגלגל העליון המקיף את הכול
sources.says: Maimonides says this verse means the one who rules over ערבות, the highest sphere that surrounds everything.

sources.quote: כמו שהרוכב מהלך בהמה כך האל יתברך מסבב הגלגל
sources.says: Radak says just as a rider drives an animal, so God turns the heavenly sphere.

68:7.headline: בכושרות: freed from chains, or freed in a fitting month?
68:7.body: Rashi reads it from כשר, fit: God took Israel out of Egypt in a month fit for travel, neither hot nor cold. Radak and Ibn Ezra read it as chains, and Radak says כ and ק are made in the same part of the mouth, so it is like קשורות, bound.

sources.quote: הוֹצִיא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרַיִם בְּחֹדֶשׁ שֶׁהוּא כָּשֵׁר לְהוֹלְכֵי דְרָכִים, לֹא חַמָּה וְלֹא צִנָּה
sources.says: Rashi says God took Israel out of Egypt in a month fit for travelers, neither hot nor cold.

sources.quote: בכושרות. הם הכבולים כענין קשורות כי כ״ף והקו״ף הם ממוצא אחד
sources.says: Radak says it means those in fetters, like 'bound', since כ and ק are made in the same place in the mouth.

sources.quote: כאילו אמר: אסורים בזיקים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is as if he said 'prisoners in chains'.

68:10.headline: תניף: God waves the rain down, or lets it drip?
68:10.body: Rashi reads תניף as waving and casting rain down. Metzudat Zion reads it as dripping, like נופת, honey from the comb, and Ibn Ezra as soaking, like 'I sprinkled my bed' in Proverbs 7.

sources.quote: הֲנִיפוֹתָ וְהִטַּלְתָּ עָלֵינוּ תָּמִיד גִּשְׁמֵי נְדָבָה וּבְרָכָה
sources.says: Rashi says God waved and cast down on us rains of generosity and blessing.

sources.quote: תניף. ענין הזלה והתכה כמו ונופת צופים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means flowing and dripping, as in 'honey from the comb'.

sources.quote: ומלת תניף – תרוה, כמו: נפתי משכבי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says תניף means 'will water', as in 'I sprinkled my bed'.

68:15.headline: בפרש: kings spread out dead, or Torah spread out plain?
68:15.body: Radak reads פרש as spreading: the enemy kings lay spread out dead on the ground. Rashi reads it as making things plain, like spreading out a garment in Deuteronomy 22:17, and takes the 'kings' as Torah scholars.

sources.quote: בפרש. ענין שיטוח לומר שהכה בהם האל והנה כולם פגרים מתים על הארץ מלכים ושרים
sources.says: Radak says it means spreading out: God struck them and all of them, kings and princes, lay as corpses on the ground.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן ״וּפָרְשׂוּ אֶת הַשִּׂמְלָה״ (דברים כב:יז), בּוֹרְרִין אֶת הַדָּבָר כְּשִׂמְלָה חֲדָשָׁה
sources.says: Rashi says it is like 'they shall spread out the garment': making a matter clear like a new garment.

sources.quote: מְלָכִים. אֵלּוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
sources.says: Rashi says the kings are Torah scholars.

68:16.headline: A mountain of peaks, named from גב, a high back
68:16.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion take גבננים from גב, anything high, and Metzudat Zion says the extra נ letters make it smaller in sense. Ibn Ezra wonders, unsure, if it comes from גבן, hunchbacked.

sources.quote: גַּבְנֻנִּים. לְשׁוֹן הָרִים, עַל שֵׁם גָּבְהָם
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word for mountains, named for their height.

sources.quote: כָּל דָּבָר גָּבוֹהַּ קָרוּי גַּב
sources.says: Rashi says anything high is called גב.

sources.quote: גבנונים. מל׳ גב וגובה והנוני״ן באים להקטין
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from גב, height, and the נ letters come to make it smaller.

sources.quote: הר גבנונים - מגזרת או גבן או דק, אולי ככה הוא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it may come from 'hunchbacked or a dwarf', perhaps.

68:22.headline: The 'hairy crown' is Esau, the hairy man
68:22.body: Rashi stops on שער, hair, and reads 'the hairy crown' as Esau, who was 'a hairy man' in Genesis 27:11. Radak reads it plainly as the top of the head, where the hair parts.

sources.quote: קָדְקֳדוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו שֶׁהוּא אִישׁ שָׂעִיר
sources.says: Rashi says it is the crown of Esau's head, since he is a hairy man.

sources.quote: כי בקדקד הראש יחלק שער הראש חציו לימין וחציו לשמאל
sources.says: Radak says at the crown the hair of the head parts, half to the right and half to the left.

68:28.headline: רגמתם: stoning them, gathering them, or their purple robes?
68:28.body: Rashi reads it as stoning: the princes envied Benjamin and threw stones at them. He also cites Menachem, who reads it as רקמתם, purple embroidery, while Radak reads 'their gathering' in Jerusalem.

sources.quote: מִתְקַנְּאִים בָּהֶם וְזוֹרְקִין בָּהֶם אֲבָנִים
sources.says: Rashi says they were jealous of them and threw stones at them.

sources.quote: רִקְמָתָם לְשׁוֹן אַרְגָּמָן, כָּךְ חִבְּרוֹ מְנַחֵם
sources.says: Rashi says Menachem grouped it with purple cloth, as their embroidery.

sources.quote: רגמתם. קיבוצם כלומר כי בירושלים נתקבצו כולם
sources.says: Radak says it means their gathering: they all gathered in Jerusalem.

68:31.headline: The beast of the reeds, or a troop of spears?
68:31.body: Rashi reads חית קנה as a wild beast living among the reeds, meaning Amalek. Radak and Meiri read קנה as a spear and חית as a company: a troop of spearmen.

sources.quote: זֶה עֲמָלֵק שֶׁנִּמְשַׁל כְּחַיַּת יַעַר הַדָּר בֵּין הַקָּנִים
sources.says: Rashi says this is Amalek, likened to a forest beast that lives among the reeds.

sources.quote: קנה הוא הרומח כלומר עדת הרמחים שנלחמים ברמחים
sources.says: Radak says קנה is a spear: the company that fights with spears.

sources.quote: וחית פירושו עדת וקנה הוא כענין רומח
sources.says: Meiri says חית means a company and קנה means a spear.

68:36.headline: 'From your sanctuaries' read as 'from your holy ones'
68:36.body: Rashi cites a midrash that reads the same letters with other vowels: not 'from your sanctuaries' but 'from your holy ones'. When God judges the righteous, as with Aaron's two sons, He is feared and exalted.

sources.quote: אַל תִּקְרֵי מִמִּקְדָּשֶׁיךָ אֶלָּא מִמְּקֻדָּשֶׁיךָ
sources.says: Rashi says: do not read 'from your sanctuaries' but 'from your holy ones'.

sources.quote: שֶׁכְּשֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשֶׂה דִּין בַּצַּדִּיקִים מִתְיָרֵא וּמִתְעַלֶּה וּמִתְקַלֵּס
sources.says: Rashi says when God judges the righteous, He is feared, exalted and praised.

sources.quote: בְּמִיתַת שְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן
sources.says: Rashi says this happened at the death of Aaron's two sons.

69:1.headline: Roses among thorns, or a lily-shaped instrument
69:1.body: Rashi reads שושנים as Israel, a rose among thorns that keep piercing it. Metzudat Zion reads it as the name of a musical instrument shaped like a lily.

sources.quote: עַל שׁוֹשַׁנִּים. עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם ״כְּשׁוֹשַׁנָּה בֵּין הַחוֹחִים״ (שיר השירים ב:ב), שֶׁהַחוֹחִים מְנַקְּבִין אוֹתָם
sources.says: Rashi says the 'roses' are Israel, like a rose among thorns that pierce it.

sources.quote: שושנים. שם כלי נגון עשויה בצורת שושנה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says שושנים is a musical instrument made in the shape of a lily.

69:3.headline: Nothing left that holds me up
69:3.body: מעמד appears only here. Radak and Meiri read it as 'something that holds up'. The drowning speaker means none of his limbs can keep him standing.

sources.quote: ומעמד פועל מבנין הפעיל, ופירושו ואין אחד מאברי שהוא מעמד
sources.says: Radak says מעמד is a causing form: not one of my limbs holds me up.

sources.quote: ואין מעמד ר״ל שאין אחד מאיבריו יכול לעמוד
sources.says: Meiri says it means none of his limbs can stand.

69:5.headline: Enemies by lies, or enemies for no reason
69:5.body: שקר usually means 'lie'. Rashi reads it that way: they hate me over a falsehood. Radak reads it like חנם, 'for no reason', matching 'those who hate me without cause' earlier in the verse.

sources.quote: אֹיְבַי שֶׁקֶר. שׂוֹנְאִים אוֹתִי עַל שֶׁקֶר
sources.says: Rashi says they hate the speaker over a lie.

sources.quote: שקר. כמו חנם
sources.says: Radak says שקר here is like חנם, for nothing.

69:6.headline: 'My folly' here means my sins
69:6.body: אולת means 'foolishness'. Metzudat Zion says it here means sins, because no one sins unless a spirit of folly comes into him.

sources.quote: לאולתי. מל׳ אויל ור״ל עבירות כי אין אדם עובר עבירה אא״כ נכנס בו רוח שטות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says 'my folly' means sins, since a person sins only when a spirit of folly enters him.

69:7.headline: Lord of which hosts: heaven's or Israel's?
69:7.body: צבאות means 'hosts' or 'armies'. Radak and Ibn Ezra read it two ways at once. God rules the hosts of heaven, and also Israel, his host on earth.

sources.quote: כי הוא אדון צבאות שמים שהגזירות יוצאות משם ברצונו והוא אדון צבאות ישראל
sources.says: Radak says God is lord of the hosts of heaven, where decrees come from, and lord of the hosts of Israel.

sources.quote: אלהי ישראל - שהם צבאותיו בארץ
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Israel are God's hosts on earth.

69:9.headline: Who are the brothers who treat him as a stranger?
69:9.body: The commentators stop on 'my brothers' and 'my mother's sons' to say who they are. Rashi says Esau. Radak, who reads the psalm as about exile, says the sons of Ishmael and the sons of Esau.

sources.quote: לְאֶחָי. לְעֵשָׂו
sources.says: Rashi says 'my brother' is Esau.

sources.quote: לאחי. הם בני ישמעאל
sources.says: Radak says 'my brothers' are the sons of Ishmael.

sources.quote: לבני אמי. הם בני עשו
sources.says: Radak says 'my mother's sons' are the sons of Esau.

69:16.headline: Don't let the pit shut its mouth on me
69:16.body: תאטר appears only here and means 'shut'. Rashi links it to a man in Judges called אטר יד ימינו: his right hand was 'shut', meaning he did not use it.

sources.quote: תֶּאְטַר. כְּמוֹ ״אִטֵּר יַד יְמִינוֹ״ (שופטים ג:טו) – סָגוּר יַד יְמִינוֹ, שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi says the word is like 'closed of his right hand' in Judges, a hand that is not used.

sources.quote: תאטר. תסגור, ואם יסגור פי הבאר אין לי מוציא ממנו
sources.says: Radak says it means 'close': if the pit's mouth closes, no one can get me out.

69:27.headline: Not the slain, but those struck nearly to death
69:27.body: חלל usually means someone killed. Radak says it cannot mean that here. The enemies want to cause pain, and no one can cause pain to the dead. So it means those wounded close to death.

sources.quote: וחלליך אינו רוצה לומר שמת לגמרי שלא יכאיב אדם המת אלא קרוב למיתה
sources.says: Radak says חלליך does not mean fully dead, since one cannot pain a dead person, but near death.

69:29.headline: God's 'book of life' is a figure of speech
69:29.body: Maimonides says the 'book of life' is not a real book that God writes in and erases. It is a picture. Ibn Ezra says the book is the heavens, where every future decree was written at creation.

sources.quote: כל אלה על דרך הדימוי, לא שיש לה' יתעלה ספר שהוא כותב בו ומוחק
sources.says: Maimonides says this verse and others like it are metaphors, not a book God writes in and erases.

sources.quote: כי ספר החיים הם השמים ושם כל הגזירות העתידות להיותם כתובות ביום הבראם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the book of life is the heavens, where all future decrees were written when they were created.

69:32.headline: Horns before hooves: Adam's ox, or simply a grown bull
69:32.body: מקרן מפריס means 'horned and hoofed'. Rashi says it is the ox Adam offered: created full-grown, it rose head-first from the earth, so its horns came before its hooves. Radak reads it simply as a grown bull, old enough to offer.

sources.quote: מַקְרִן מַפְרִיס. קַרְנוֹתָיו קָדְמוּ לְפַרְסוֹתָיו, שֶׁהֲרֵי בְּקוֹמָתוֹ וּבְקַרְנָיו נִבְרָא, וְרֹאשׁוֹ יָצָא מִן הָאָרֶץ תְּחִלָּה
sources.says: Rashi says the ox's horns came before its hooves, because it was created full-size and its head came out of the earth first.

sources.quote: מקרין מפריס. טעמו על הפר שהוא בעל קרנים ופרסותיו חזקות כי קודם שיהיו לו קרנים פרסותיו רכות
sources.says: Radak says it describes a bull with horns and hard hooves, since before its horns grow its hooves are soft.

7:1.headline: שגיון: a kind of song, or a confession of a mistake?
7:1.body: Menachem, cited by Rashi, says שגיון names a kind of song or instrument. The sages read it from the word for an error: David prays about his mistake toward Saul.

sources.quote: מְנַחֵם אָמַר שֶׁגַּם זֶה אֶחָד מִשְּׁמוֹת הַזֶּמֶר עַל שֵׁם הַכְּלִי
sources.says: Rashi cites Menachem: this is one of the names for a song, taken from an instrument.

sources.quote: וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ פֵּרְשׁוּ לְשׁוֹן מִשְׁגֶּה
sources.says: Rashi says our sages explained it from the word for an error.

sources.quote: התפלל בזה על השגיאה מה שכרת כנף מעיל שאול
