sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'all gods' means the angels of heaven, because they are his messengers.

sources.quote: אלהים. הם מלאכי מעלה
sources.says: Metzudat David says the word means the angels above.

sources.quote: והם צבא השמים שהם אלהים ושופטים בארץ
sources.says: Radak says it means the host of heaven, which act as powers and judges over the earth.

sources.quote: וכי יש אלקים אחרים והרי הוא אומר
sources.says: The Midrash asks whether there are other gods, since the Torah says there are none besides him.

95:6.headline: Our Maker, or the one who makes us great
95:6.body: עושנו usually means 'who made us', but Radak and Metzudat Zion read it as 'who raises us up and makes us great'. Ibn Ezra keeps the plain sense: he made the sea and the land, and all that is in them.

sources.quote: מגדלנו ומרוממנו כי הוא שופטנו
sources.says: Radak says it means the one who makes us great and raises us up, because he is our judge.

sources.quote: ענין הרמה וגדולה כמו הוא עשך ויכוננך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means raising up and greatness, as in 'he made you and established you' in Deuteronomy.

sources.quote: כי עשה הים והיבשה והם כללים ומהם עשה הפרטים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it refers to God making the sea and the dry land, and from them all the details.

95:7.headline: The flock of his hand: led by a wave, not a stick
95:7.body: Metzudat David says a kind shepherd leads his sheep with a motion of his hand, not with a stick. Ibn Ezra links the hand to verse 5, where his hands formed the dry land.

sources.quote: כמו הרועה הרחמני אשר ינהג הצאן עם נטיית היד ולא במקל
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is like a merciful shepherd who leads the flock by moving his hand, not with a stick.

sources.quote: וצאן ידו - כנגד ידיו יצרו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'his hand' matches 'his hands formed' the dry land in verse 5.

95:9.headline: My deeds: the miracles they saw, or the punishment they got
95:9.body: Rashi and Radak say 'my deeds' are the miracles: Egypt, the split sea, the manna. Ibn Ezra says the deed they saw was their own punishment, since they all died in the desert.

sources.quote: גַּם רָאוּ פָעֳלִי. בְּמִצְרָיִם
sources.says: Rashi says the deeds they saw were in Egypt.

sources.quote: גם ראו שבקעתי להם הים והמן שהורדתי להם
sources.says: Radak says they saw that God split the sea for them and brought down the manna.

sources.quote: וטעם ראו פעלי – שמתו כולם במדבר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'they saw my deeds' means they all died in the desert.

95:11.headline: 'If they enter' is an oath that means 'they never will'
95:11.body: אם usually means 'if', but Radak and Metzudat David say it is the language of an oath. The speaker leaves the curse unsaid, so 'if they enter' means 'they will never enter'.

sources.quote: ופירוש אם. בדרך שבועה כמו שאדם אומר יהיה כך וכך אם יהיה זה
sources.says: Radak says אם is the form of an oath, like a person saying 'let such-and-such happen if this happens'.

sources.quote: אם יבואון. ענין שבועה הוא וגזם ולא אמר
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is an oath, with the threat left unspoken.

96:1.headline: Why a "new song"? Rashi says it points to the future
96:1.body: Rashi says that wherever the Tanach says "new song", it speaks of the time to come. Radak and Meiri say it means a song beyond the old psalms, for wonders not yet sung about.

sources.quote: בְּכָל מָקוֹם שִׁיר חָדָשׁ עַל הֶעָתִיד
sources.says: Rashi says that everywhere, "new song" refers to the future.

sources.quote: שתתחדשו לו שיר זולתי המזמורים והשירים הנכתבים
sources.says: Radak says it means to make up a new song for God beyond the psalms and songs already written.

sources.quote: ולא יספיקו לכם השירים והמזמורים והתהלות שנעשו
sources.says: Meiri says the songs already made will not be enough for all the wonders God will do.

96:1.headline: "All the earth": every nation, or the land of Israel?
96:1.body: Radak and Meiri say it means everyone who lives on the earth. Ibn Ezra, at verse 3, says that since the nations are named separately there, "all the earth" is the land of Israel.

sources.quote: כל הארץ. כל יושבי הארץ
sources.says: Radak says "all the earth" means all who live on the earth.

sources.quote: וכל הארץ ר״ל כל יושבי הארץ
sources.says: Meiri says it means all who live on the earth.

sources.quote: בעבור שהזכיר בגוים, על כן כל הארץ הוא ארץ ישראל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says that because the verse mentions "the nations", "all the earth" is the land of Israel.

96:2.headline: Why keep announcing news everyone already knows?
96:2.body: בשרו means to bring fresh news. Radak says the rescue should feel new each day, as sweet as on the day it was first heard.

sources.quote: יהיה סיפור הישועה חביבה בעיניהם בכל יום ויום כאילו נהיתה אז
sources.says: Radak says the story of the rescue will be dear to them every day, as if it had just happened.

sources.quote: בשרו. ענינו השמעת חדשות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means telling news.

96:4.headline: Feared above all "gods": angels, or sun and stars?
96:4.body: Radak and Ibn Ezra say the "gods" here are the angels. Metzudat David and Meiri say they are the sun, moon and stars that idol worshippers served.

sources.quote: על כל אלהים - הם המלאכים, כי הוא אלהי האלהים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the gods are the angels, for God is the God of gods.

sources.quote: אלהים. הם המלאכי' יגדלוהו
sources.says: Radak says these are the angels, who will praise him.

sources.quote: הם השמש והירח וכל צבא השמים שהיו העובדי גלולים עובדים להם
sources.says: Metzudat David says these are the sun, moon and stars that idol worshippers served.

96:5.headline: The nations' gods are אלילים, a word built from "not"
96:5.body: Metzudat Zion says אלילים comes from אל and לא, two words for "not": a thing that does nothing. Ibn Ezra calls it emptiness and falsehood, as in "worthless doctors" in Job.

sources.quote: הוא מלשון אל ולא, ר״ל דבר מבלי תועלת
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from אל and לא, and means a thing without use.

sources.quote: שוא ושקר כמו רופאי אליל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means emptiness and falsehood, as in "worthless doctors".

96:6.headline: "His sanctuary": the heavens, or the Temple with the Ark?
96:6.body: Radak says the sanctuary is the heavens, where the stars give God honor. Ibn Ezra prefers the Temple, where the Ark, which is called "strength", stood.

sources.quote: יתנו במקדשו והוא השמים שהם מעון קדשו
sources.says: Radak says his sanctuary is the heavens, his holy dwelling.

sources.quote: או הארון שנקרא עוז בבית המקדש והוא הנכון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it may be the heavens, or the Ark in the Temple, which is called "strength", and that the Ark is right.

96:11.headline: Does the sea really roar, or is it a picture of joy?
96:11.body: Ibn Ezra says the roar may be thunder from clouds rising off the sea, or music like that played for a king coming home. Radak says it is all a picture of the world's great joy.

sources.quote: העננים העולים מהים או הכל דרך משל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it may be the clouds rising from the sea, or all a figure of speech, or like musicians going out before a king returning from far away.

sources.quote: הכל דרך משל על שמחה הגדולה
sources.says: Radak says the joy of the heavens, earth, sea and trees is all a figure for the great joy that will come.

sources.quote: לְהָרִים קוֹל בִּתְהִלָּה
sources.says: Rashi says it means to raise a voice in praise.

96:12.headline: Forest trees singing: real trees, or rulers of nations?
96:12.body: Rashi reads the trees as the rulers of the nations. Radak and Meiri read the singing trees as a picture of great joy in a world at peace.

sources.quote: כָּל שָׁלְטוֹנֵי הָאֻמּוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says the trees of the forest are all the rulers of the nations.

sources.quote: אז ירננו עצי היער הכל משל לשמחה גדולה לרוב השלוה
sources.says: Meiri says the singing trees are a figure for great joy because of the great peace.

sources.quote: ורננת העצים, הכל דרך משל
sources.says: Radak says the singing of the trees is a figure of speech.

97:1.headline: "The LORD reigns": a past-tense verb about the future
97:1.body: The verb is in the past tense, yet Meiri says it speaks of a redemption still to come, as prophecy always does. Rashi ties it to the day God takes the kingdom away from Amalek.

sources.quote: וה׳ מלך עבר במקום עתיד כי כן דרכי הנבואה תמיד
sources.says: Meiri says "reigns" is a past tense standing for the future, which is always the way of prophecy.

sources.quote: בְּנָטְלוֹ הַמְּלוּכָה מֵעֲמָלֵק וּמִזַּרְעוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means when God takes the kingdom from Amalek and his descendants.

sources.quote: לעתיד כאשר תתגלה מלכותו
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is about the future, when God's kingship is revealed.

97:2.headline: Cloud around God: darkness for the wicked, or our own limits?
97:2.body: Radak and Metzudat David read the cloud as darkness sent against the wicked. Maimonides says God is not wrapped in fog: the cloud stands for the matter we are made of, which keeps us from grasping him.

sources.quote: להסב את תשומת הלב לכך שהמונע הוא עכירות העצם שלנו, לא שהוא יתעלה גוף שמקיף אותו ערפל
sources.says: Maimonides says the verse shows that what blocks us is the murkiness of our own being, not that God is a body wrapped in fog.

sources.quote: להחשיך ולהקדיר על הרשעים
sources.says: Radak says the cloud and fog bring darkness on the wicked.

sources.quote: הוא משל לחשכת הצרות שיהיו מוכנים לענוש בהם את הרשעים
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is a picture of dark troubles made ready to punish the wicked.

97:5.headline: Mountains melting like wax: the proud kings of the earth
97:5.body: Radak and Meiri read the mountains as the kings of the nations. Ibn Ezra says they are the proud, and notes that dry mountains melting goes against nature.

sources.quote: והרים. הוא משל על מלכי הרשעים
sources.says: Radak says the mountains are a figure for wicked kings.

sources.quote: והרים ר״ל מלכי ארץ שהם מלכי האומות ושריהם וגדוליהם
sources.says: Meiri says the mountains are the kings of the nations, their princes and their great men.

sources.quote: הם המתגאים ואמרו נמסו, אע"פ שהם יבשים הפך התולדת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they are the proud, and the verse says they melted though they are dry, against nature.

97:6.headline: How do the heavens "tell"? Through angels, or through hail
97:6.body: Ibn Ezra and the Targum say the ones who tell are those who live in heaven, the angels. Radak says the heavens tell by raining hail and fire on the wicked.

sources.quote: הגידו - יושבי שמים, כי הם עושים דברי השם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is those who live in heaven, who carry out God's word.

sources.quote: יְתַנוּן אַנְגְלֵי מְרוֹמָא צִדְקְתֵיהּ
sources.says: The Targum says "the angels on high will tell his righteousness".

sources.quote: השמים בהמטירם אבני חלגביש ואש גפרית על הרשעים יגידו צדק האל
sources.says: Radak says that when the heavens rain hailstones and burning sulfur on the wicked, they announce God's justice.

97:6.headline: צדק: fairness in punishing, or kindness to Israel?
97:6.body: Meiri says the word צדק can mean kindness or uprightness. Here it may be God's fairness in punishing the nations, or his kindness, since those judgments are kindness to Israel.

sources.quote: ומלת צדק תבא לפעמים כענין חסד ופעמים כענין יושר
sources.says: Meiri says the word צדק sometimes means kindness and sometimes uprightness.

sources.quote: או יהיה צדקו כענין חסדו כי משפטיו על האומות הם חסד לישראל
sources.says: Meiri says "his righteousness" may mean his kindness, because his judgments on the nations are kindness to Israel.

97:7.headline: "All gods bow to him": the stars, or their worshippers?
97:7.body: Radak says these "gods" are the hosts of heaven that people worshipped, or else the worshippers themselves, as the Targum reads it. Ibn Ezra reports some who say they are angels.

sources.quote: הם צבא השמים שהם נעבדים הם יודו וישתחוו לה'
sources.says: Radak says these are the hosts of heaven that were worshipped, and they will bow to God.

sources.quote: או פירושו כל אלהים. כל עובדי אלהים אחרים
sources.says: Radak says it may instead mean all who serve other gods.

sources.quote: כָּל עַמַיָא פַּלְחֵי טַעֲוָתָא
sources.says: The Targum says "all the peoples who serve idols".

sources.quote: יש אומרים: כי כל אלהים הם המלאכים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports that some say "all gods" are the angels.

97:11.headline: Light "sown" for the righteous, or light that shines?
97:11.body: Rashi reads it as real sowing, ready to sprout, and Ibn Ezra adds that a little sown yields much. Meiri reads זרוע as זרוח, "shines", because the letters ע and ח can swap.

sources.quote: זְרִיעָה מַמָּשׁ, מוּכֶנֶת לִצְמֹחַ לָהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it is real sowing, ready to sprout for them.

sources.quote: טעם זרוע - אם זרע מעט יקצור הרבה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means sown: whoever sows a little reaps a lot.

sources.quote: וזרוע הוא כמו זרוח כי אותיות ה״ח ע״א מתחלפות
sources.says: Meiri says זרוע is like זרוח, shining, because the letters ה, ח, ע and א can replace each other.

98:1.headline: 'His right hand saved him': does God need saving?
98:1.body: The verse says God's own hand brought Him victory, as if He needed help. Metzudat David says the point is that God needs no help from anyone else. Meiri says it reads as if God Himself needed saving, and compares it to 'in all their troubles He was troubled' in Isaiah 63.

sources.quote: אינו צריך תשועה מזולתו כי ימינו הושיעה לו
sources.says: Metzudat David says God needs no help from another, because His own right hand saved Him.

sources.quote: פי׳ כאלו היה הוא צריך תשועה שבגאולת העם הנבחר
sources.says: Meiri says it is as if God Himself needed saving when His chosen people were rescued.

sources.quote: והוא כענין בכל צרתם לו צר
sources.says: Meiri says this is like the verse 'in all their troubles He was troubled'.

sources.quote: הושיעה לו ימינו, כמו: ותושע לי זרועי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra compares it to 'my own arm brought me victory' in Isaiah.

98:5.headline: Why 'with the harp' twice: alone, then with singing
98:5.body: The word 'with the harp' comes twice in a row. Ibn Ezra, Radak and Metzudat David say the first is the harp played alone, and the second is the harp with a singing voice.

sources.quote: בכנור לבדו וכן בכנור עם קול זמרה שהוא שיר בפה
sources.says: Radak says it means with the harp alone, and also with the harp together with a voice singing.

sources.quote: בכנור - לבדו, ובכנור וקול זמרה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the first is the harp alone, and the second the harp with the sound of song.

sources.quote: בכנור לבד גם בכנור עם קול זמרה יחד לבסם את הקול
sources.says: Metzudat David says first the harp alone, then the harp with singing, to sweeten the sound.

98:8.headline: 'Rivers' clap: the water itself, or the people who sail it
98:8.body: Meiri first reads the rivers as a picture, as if they were alive and clapping for joy. Ibn Ezra and Meiri also read 'rivers' as the people who travel on the seas and rivers, who will sing.

sources.quote: משל לרוב שמחה כאילו הם בעלי חיים
sources.says: Meiri says the clapping rivers are a picture of great joy, as if they were living things.

sources.quote: או נפרש נהרות יורדי הים והולכי דרך נהר
sources.says: Meiri says 'rivers' may also mean those who go down to the sea and travel by river.

sources.quote: הטעם כי בני אדם שהם בספינות הים ובנהרות ובהרים ירונו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means the people on ships at sea, on the rivers and in the mountains will sing.

99:1.headline: A word found nowhere else for the earth's quaking
99:1.body: תָּנוּט appears only here. Ibn Ezra says it means 'shake' and has no partner word. Rashi links it to נָטָיוּ, 'my feet slipped'; Meiri links it to wobbling, since ד and ט are made in the same part of the mouth.

sources.quote: תנוט הארץ - כמו: תרעש ואין חבר לו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means 'will shake' and the word has no other example.

sources.quote: תָּנוּט. לְשׁוֹן ״נָטָיוּ רַגְלָי״
sources.says: Rashi links it to 'my feet had almost slipped' in Psalms 73:2.

sources.quote: שתרעד ותתנועע ותתנודד כי הדלת והטית ממוצא אחד
sources.says: Meiri reads it as tremble and sway, since the letters dalet and tet are said in the same place.

99:5.headline: God's footstool is the Temple
99:5.body: A הֲדֹם is a footstool under the feet of someone seated. Here the commentators read it as the Temple, or the Ark inside it: as if God sits in heaven and rests his feet on earth.

sources.quote: הוא שרפרף הכסא הנתון תחת רגלי היושב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means the stool set under the feet of one sitting on a chair.

sources.quote: ואחז במשל כאלו ממכון שבתו השמים יוריד רגליו לנוח בבה״‎מ
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is a picture: from his seat in heaven, God lowers his feet to rest in the Temple.

sources.quote: לנגד מקום הארון כי מקום הדומו קדוש הוא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says to bow toward the place of the Ark, because his footstool is holy.
